#844. Lise Klaveness: ‘Certainly there are people that can challenge Infantino’

Norwegian federation president distances self from Fifa presidency but believes governing body can be reformed

As the rain whips around Oslo’s government quarter, Lise Klaveness is shielding herself from the wind, trying to work out tactics. “Of course we cannot probably do everything alone, but we have a voice, we have the right to speak, we have the right to suggest, so let’s see,” she says. “We will at least try to be a spearhead.”

The president of the Norwegian Football Federation wants to re-engage Fifa, and other governing bodies, on the topic of remedy. A slightly arcane aspect of human rights policy in normal times, the importance of remedy became very clear in the aftermath of the World Cup in Qatar, when the families of those injured or killed in the work that led up to the tournament were left without financial compensation after Fifa chose to direct a legacy fund elsewhere.

At Klaveness’s prompting, Fifa conducted a review into the process. The report ultimately found the organisation did have a responsibility to provide remedy, but Fifa chose not to redirect the money. Klaveness wants to focus minds on the topic once again and make sure new practices are in place for Euro 2028, co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, as well as the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia, where labour movement sources suggest there is little to no external scrutiny on worker’s conditions.

She is doing so at a delicate juncture. While Gianni Infantino has assured those listening that the “vast, vast majority” of Fifa’s electorate will back his re-election as president next year, many within the game regard this as an opportunity for change. Klaveness is one of them, having been a thorn in Infantino’s side since she first raised the topic of remedy on the floor of the Fifa congress in 2022 and having called for him to resign this summer after the scandals of the Balogun red card and the Fifa Forward Enterprise fiasco.

The 45-year-old Klaveness has been touted as a possible candidate in the Fifa presidential election, earning a perhaps less than desirable endorsement from Sepp Blatter. The disgraced former president said Klaveness “deserved the utmost respect” and that “the time has come for a woman to take over the leadership”. Klaveness responded by recalling that Blatter “wanted us to play with shorter shorts”. Her position on a run for president today is to almost, if not entirely, rule it out.

“My name has come up a few times and I take it as a sign that [people are concerned] about governance because we have been very outspoken about governance,” she says. “We’ve had a role internationally that is not the most efficient way to get votes. I think we’ve been very outspoken so this time around I don’t think that would be a possibility for me and it’s not been a real subject for me either.”

Not quite a no, then, but whether she runs or not Klaveness is a consistent champion for reform. She believes there are other candidates out there who could challenge Infantino and deliver change. She says it is crucial that any such individual is persuaded to stand before the deadline for nominations on 18 November. “It’s really important to have a candidate and one who can win,” she says. “We will welcome any candidate, but just putting up somebody who will lose is …” She shrugs. “I think it’s important to now discuss who can have a platform to win.

“There has been distrust, and not just in Europe, many other places than Europe,” she says of the challenge to Infantino. “Of course, it’s become very political, that’s why I refer to it as the Game of Thrones. Candidates need to have a base in different confederations. We don’t know how challenged Infantino can be until there’s a counter-candidate like that. But certainly there are people that can challenge him.”

On this day at least Klaveness is reluctant to make too many pugnacious remarks about Infantino or Fifa. “People ask me all the time about Infantino, but it’s not about him,” she says. “For me it’s about the governance going forward. He was elected on a platform of reform, which we really believed in, but it was not really implemented and that disappointed us.”

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Klaveness says she wants any reforms around remedy to apply to all organisers and competitions. She talks about building alliances to back proposals that would ensure funds are set aside for remedy before a tournament takes place and that mechanisms are established for how any money should be distributed. She wants to submit such proposals at the next Fifa congress. “It should also be in Uefa and other places, but let’s start with Fifa, let’s start at the top, and now that governance is on everybody’s lips let’s make this part of the suggestions we will make to the congress, together or alone.”

A collaborative approach to achieving solutions, rather than deals struck behind closed doors, is Klaveness’s preferred way and on Tuesday the former midfielder, with 73 Norway caps, made her case on remedy to a gathering of politicians commemorating the 50th anniversary of the OECD’s guidelines for “responsible business conduct”. No longer the lone voice speaking out on the conference floor, Klaveness has allies and a growing number of people who – at least in private – would claim to share her values. That she also presides over two successful national sides doesn’t hurt.

Norway’s women’ face a playoff against Wales to qualify for next year’s World Cup. The men, meanwhile, won hearts and matches in the US this year. Klaveness recalls with some bemusement the World Cup experience. “I was on the road for seven weeks with 65 men,” she says. “I also saw Erling Haaland with a dead raccoon. Football is a lot of things, a sport, a competition, a cultural phenomenon. It’s also a social tool, but if we want the game to be for everyone there is going to be conflict.” It won’t be too long before that conflict resumes.

#843. How landmark Everton compensation prevented Burnley record loss

Burnley were bought by ALK Capital in December 2020 using loans secured against the club's assets and other external debt

Six years ago, Burnley were considered one of the best-run clubs in the country.

The Clarets were debt free, with Â£41.65m cash in the bank, and enjoying their fifth successive season of Premier League football.

Now they sit in the Championship relegation zone, with concerns over debt and the way the Clarets were bought by ALK Capital using loans and the club's own money.

Fans have been very concerned about what the future holds - although on Wednesday there was some rare positive news in the club's accounts.

BBC Sport takes a closer look at what is going on at Turf Moor.

You may be familiar with the term "leverage buyout" after the Glazer family's purchase of Manchester United in 2005.

It effectively means that a purchase is carried out using debt secured on the club's assets, its own bank balance and other loans, rather than the equity of the buyer.

In Burnley's case, ALK Capital took out a Â£65m loan secured against the club's assets, such as Turf Moor, and used Â£37m from the club's own bank balance.

On top of that, Velocity Capital, the holding company, owed Burnley Â£80.1m - money which was also used to buy the club.

The original Â£65m loan was partially paid off, but then refinanced and extended to reach Â£105m in the 2024-25 accounts. Interest rates were as high as 12%.

On top of that were factored debts, when a club mortgages off future transfer instalments for a one-off payment from the bank. Burnley owed Â£37m at an interest rate of 12.75%.

In total, the football club's borrowings stood at Â£142.3m, the 10th-highest external debt in English football.

Then came the 2025-26 accounts, published today, which painted a different picture.

Now, back to that leveraged buyout which has been attracting so much criticism from fans.

Last season's accounts contained a big surprise.

Remember Velocity Capital, the holding company that owed Burnley Â£80.1m for the purchase of the club?

The accounts revealed Â£77.7m of that has now been paid to the Clarets.

It cleared a large chunk of the debt used to buy the football club and helped to make the latest accounts look healthier.

This was needed because, over the past six years, debts related to the leveraged buyout and associated interest payments had increased.

The Â£77.7m payment, funded by investment from the ownership group, does not mean all Burnley's financial concerns or debts have been resolved.

The club still reported a loss for 2025-26 of Â£9m, compared with Â£24m-Â£29m in the previous three seasons.

But this includes the Velocity Capital payment, money for being in the Premier League - and a landmark compensation payout.

The Clarets have been paid Â£38.8m by Everton because of the Toffees' profit and sustainability breach in 2021-22, which was found to have impacted Burnley's chances of avoiding relegation that season.

Crucially, however, the payout is subject to an appeal, which is expected to be heard in January.

In the accounts, the board stated that "no provision should be included" for the appeal, the result of which could "range between Â£Nil and the full value of the award detailed being repayable".

This, the club argues, is because "the outcome of the appeal cannot be reasonably determined or measured".

Without the Everton payment, the loss in the 2025-26 accounts would have been Â£47.8m rather than Â£9m - a record loss for the club despite it reporting all-time high revenues of Â£144.5m for the campaign.

Removing the Everton payment might present a more realistic picture of their finances.

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool, told BBC Sport that the timing of the accounts is noteworthy, too, coming six months earlier than expected.

"It was a surprise that Burnley filed their accounts now, but it makes sense considering the Everton payment and pending appeal," Maguire said.

"If Everton are successful, and Burnley were to file their accounts next April, the Â£38.8m could not be included the 2025-26 accounts. So by reporting early, Burnley can include it and avoid potentially recording the record loss."

Premier League football has been seen as key to Burnley's finances - but the accounts show even in the top flight things were a struggle financially.

"The underlying features are that the club was still losing effectively more than Â£1m a week," Maguire said.

"That was despite the benefits of being in the Premier League, and therefore relying on player sales and the Everton settlement to reduce the figures to something more palatable."

Burnley supporters have been protesting against the ownership of Alan Pace's ALK Capital for much of the season

The three influxes of money helped reduce the debt, and heavy interest repayments.

The club's debt now stands at Â£62.9m, more than half what it was in 2024-25.

But remember, Burnley had been debt free before the takeover.

Bank loans have reduced from Â£105m to Â£70.1m.

Burnley had also, in recent seasons, mortgaged off future transfer instalments for a one-off payment from the bank, called 'debt factoring'.

Previously at Â£37m, they reduced it to Â£16.1m.

This all looks good, but is still reliant on the payment from Everton. If the Toffees do win their appeal, the picture looks very different.

Added to that, Â£24.2m of the bank loans is due for repayment in January, with another Â£21.6m falling next August.

The club is in "negotiations to refinance and increase these facilities", but the accounts note that if an agreement is not reached the owners will require "additional finance to repay the amounts due".

What about next season? It will be a season in the Championship, with much lower revenues and no one-off payment from Everton.

The 2026-27 accounts will include player sales of around Â£38m and parachute payments of Â£48m.

On the face of it, the numbers look very encouraging for Burnley.

But the accounts laid out that a number of events, including "the outcome of the ongoing compensation ruling appeal", could continue to "cast significant doubt" on the club as a going concern.

Maguire added: "A more forensic look suggests that the underlying issues at Burnley still exist.

"Given that they were in receipt of Premier League broadcast revenues and the benefits of being in the top division, that does suggest that the club faces ongoing challenges.â ââ ââ "

On the field, Burnley need a revival - and fast.

It is still early in the Championship season - 14 games have been played - but Burnley sit in the relegation zone.

Over the past six years, they have been a yo-yo club between the Premier League and the Championship, trading the riches of the top flight with strong revenues from a promotion campaign each season.

A big turnaround is needed for that to still be the case under the new management of Swiss Fabio Celestini, who is yet to win in his two games in charge.

Burnley have recorded just one victory in the opening 14 Championship games, leaving them four points adrift in the bottom three.

Recently they set a new English league record for the longest run without a home win, which will reach 400 days when arch-rivals Blackburn visit Turf Moor on 22 November.

Relegation looks more likely than promotion at the moment, and Burnley cannot afford to become the third team in successive seasons to do the double drop from the Premier League to League One.

But time will tell whether the improved results in the accounts start to be replicated on the pitch.

#842. Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny

Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

On the final day of October, what may well be the final Summer Youth Olympics ever will begin. It will be the first on African soil as around 2,700 athletes aged 15-17 arrive in Senegal to compete across a total of 153 events in 25 sports.

Hosted in eight venues across three locations – Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly, 80 kilometers (50 miles) from the capital – these Games are seen by many as a prelude to Africa hosting a full Olympics one day in the future.

"I'm really excited about the Youth Olympic Games because, for the first time, I'll be representing our country," 15-year-old judoka Aisha Diop who is competing for Senegal told DW.

"I am very proud to be able to represent my country at these Games. This will really motivate young African athletes because they will improve, and they will want to continue playing sports now that the Youth Games have been held here."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The 2026 Youth Games in Senegal will also be a first beyond the history it is making in Africa.

"Of the 2,700 athletes who will be competing in Dakar, there will be a 50-50 split between men and women," Olivia Nloga, Chief Brand Promotion Officer on the organizing committee, told DW.

"But this parity isn't just reflected in the overall figure. This gender parity will also be reflected in each event and in each sport where such parity actually exists."

Several sports are also making their debut at the Youth Olympic Games, such as five-a-side baseball, kung fu and the Senegalese specialty of beach wrestling. There's also a refugee team at the Youth Olympic Games for the first time.

"As I said earlier, the Youth Olympic Games aren't just about sports, and they aren't just about infrastructure," said Nloga.

"For us, it was also important to use this time to build on and reinforce the idea that these Games in Senegal are a celebration for the people. We did this by investing in culture—for example, through a fashion show and a program called Yi-sol, which is a mural project on the city's walls."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Other projects designed to celebrate the people include music, and a local student designed the mascot. The biggest focus of all though, is on creating sustainability for the young people of Senegal.

"We did so through a program that is very important to us – one that is close to our hearts, namely, the Olympic Civic and Sports Certificate," Nloga said.

"We traveled to schools throughout Senegal and worked with more than 1,000 instructors to reach and make an impact on more than one million young Senegalese children who, during this hiatus, were exposed to and educated about the values of the Olympic Movement."

With recent flooding in the country, there were concerns that infrastructure would have been affected, but Nloga insisted that flood risk had long been in the planning.

"The prime minister held an interdepartmental meeting during which he established a task force to ensure that the necessary arrangements and follow-up measures are put in place to safeguard both the competition venues and the accommodation sites."

With Formula 1 confirming its return to Africa earlier in October, global sport is slowly becoming a more regular event in Africa. As a result though, there have been questions asked about the legacy of such events.

Many in Senegal concerned by the high cost of living and unemployment will see these Games as an unnecessary expense. For the Senegalese authorities though, they are an opportunity for long-term investment in the country's young people as well as infrastructure. There is also the hope that this will make Dakar a major tourist destination.

There was further criticism of the Games being in Senegal from Human Rights Watch (HRW), with the NGO calling on the Senegalese authorities to change their stance on the LGBTQ+ community.

"You are welcoming all of the world. It shouldn't be 'you are welcome to our country, except this, except that,'" Larissa Kojoue from HRW told DW.

"Anti-LGBT legislation and that crackdown that is going on, they contradict the Olympic movement, the Olympic Charter, and also various human rights convention that the country has signed."

Earlier this year, Senegal President Bassirou Diomaye Faye signed into law new legislation on same-sex relations that have proved contentious abroad despite broad political support within the majority Muslim country's parliament. Several human rights groups had voiced concerns about the bill, including warning that it would dissuade people at risk of illnesses like HIV/AIDS from seeking help.

The Games were set to see the return of Russians to Olympic competition under their own colours after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) lifted their suspension in July.

However, the Russian Athletics Federation (RusAF) released a statement the day before the opening ceremony saying the reported 13 athletes (and 10 coaches) had been exluded from the competition. They demanded an explanation and asked for the decision to be reconsidered.

"The IOC-endorsed position was clear in its direction: young athletes holding Russian or Belarusian passports should no longer be restricted from international youth competitions. That principle should apply to Dakar 2026," read the statement.

Despite the IOC's ruling, each federation can still decide whether to authorize Russian participation. World Athletics, has clearly upheld their ban, while swimming and judo have allowed Russian athletes back.

"This has enabled World Athletics to pursue its own exclusory agenda in the face of clear and just directions from the IOC. This activism is only detrimental to youth sports, with the result being that Russian young athletes will be denied the opportunity to compete at these Games."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Despite the various concerns, there is an overriding hope that the Games will be prove beneficial for all involved.

"What makes the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar special is that they are also rooted in Senegal's extremely strong sporting culture," Nloga said.

"Every evening, when you take a stroll along the Corniche in Dakar, you're struck by the number of people you see exercising, regardless of their age or physical condition. What we'll be offering during these Olympic Games is also an immersion into Senegalese life – into the way sports are just as much a part of Senegalese identity."

This article was updated on October 30, 2026 to reflect the change in situation for Russian athletes at the Games.

Sira Thierij conducted interviews for this article. Edited by: Chuck Penfold

#841. Tara Lipinski Admits She's Unsure About Daughter's Skating Future

Big Bargain Holiday Showdown host Tara Lipinski shared insight into her 3-year-old daughter Georgie’s passion for skating in an exclusive E! News interview: "I just want it to be all fun."

Tara Lipinski is surprised how her daughter is skating to her own tune.

The Olympic figure skater shared that while it's been incredibly heartwarming to watch her and husband Todd Kapostasy’s 3-year-old Georgie take to the ice, she’s not sure if she wants her daughter joining the world of competitive figure skating.

“I never really want her to ever feel pressure to ever follow in my footsteps,” Lipinski exclusively told E! News. “So part of me really never thought she would skate. And I don't know if I actually want her to skate.”

However, Georgie has really found her footing on the ice, with Lipinski joking, “The problem is she likes it.”

For now, the 44-year-old is going to encourage the fun part of skating, adding that getting involved in sports is also “a great confidence builder” that can “give you so many tools that you use later in life.”

“If she loves it as much as she does, we'll do it for as long as she wants,” Lipinski said, sharing that Georgie “loves the sparkly outfits, and she loves the sequins, and skating to 'Pink Pony Club.’”

“I just want it to be all fun,” she emphasized. “I obviously saw how serious a sport can get, and for Georgie I just want her to see all the positive aspects of being on the ice and having fun.”

Of course, the Olympic gold medalist is doing her best to keep the fun skating along for Georgie, especially with the holidays coming up.

“We are in prime magical Christmas memories and moments and she is so into it,” Lipinski raved. “I even told her this morning, I was like, ‘It's time to decorate for Christmas,’ and you can see the little smile pop up.”

Luckily, she’s got plenty of inspiration for her holiday decor as the host of HGTV’s Big Bargain Holiday Showdown, in which contestants are challenged to create Christmastime magic on a dime.

“I had a little notepad that I, eventually, after the second episode, was like, ‘Oh, I'm going to take notes on this. I don't need to spend money to do that. Now I can do it like this,’” she shared. “The added benefit of the show is that we get to see how it's done on a budget and that it's relatable, so that everyone at home can try fun projects when it comes to their decorating this year.”

And the sports commentator was truly dazzled by how the competitors stuck the landing on the series, raving, “It was incredible to see how the teams were able to come up with these creative and unique ideas.”

Big Bargain Holiday Showdown airs on HGTV Tuesday nights starting Nov. 3 at 9 p.m. ET.

For a look at more shows headed to the small screen this year, keep reading.

Nocturne tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), an ex-soldier turned homicide detective who, tired of working the tough streets of Philadelphia, moves to a small town in Western Pennsylvania for a quiet life. But, as the town and his family come under attack from the diabolically cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Stephen Graham), Jonah must protect all that he holds dear. When the desperate search for Jurek’s last missing victim forces Jonah to send his surrogate daughter FBI Agent Saga Bauer (Zazie Beetz) up against Jurek, how far will Jonah go?

Bertha Russell changed Society at a cost. Now, her family must reckon with the consequences as Agnes van Rhijn seizes an opportunity to regain her position. Meanwhile, Marian forges a new path for herself, and Peggy works to be accepted by her future in-laws. In this new era, you must be careful what you wish for.

St. Denis Medical is a mockumentary about an underfunded, understaffed Oregon hospital where the dedicated doctors and nurses try their best to treat patients while maintaining their own sanity. In season three, romantic entanglements and personal struggles complicate relationships in the Emergency Department, pushing some St. Denis employees to the brink.

The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins (NBC) - Nov. 2

Season two of the hit comedy returns with the unlikely duo of former football star Reggie Dinkins (Tracy Morgan) and documentarian Arthur Tobin (Daniel Radcliffe), both still chasing redemption and still making a mess of it. With the help of his family, Reggie will continue his quest to recapture his past glory.

In season two, Santi takes the next step in his pursuit of professional golf, only to discover how quickly the game changes when talent becomes expectation. As Santi chases his dream, Pryce Cahill (Owen Wilson) finds himself wondering what might still be possible for him. Urged on by his former rival Clark Ross (Timothy Olyphant), Pryce does something nobody expects: he bets on himself, launching an improbable comeback in hopes of becoming the oldest golfer ever to win a major. But the road back proves far harder than he imagined. And the closer Pryce gets to the golfer he once was, the more he is forced to confront why he never fulfilled the promise everyone once saw in him. With brilliant new coach Amanda (Rhea Seehorn) and trusted caddie Mitts (Marc Maron) in his corner, Pryce sets out to prove — to the golf world and, more importantly, to himself — that maybe he really was as good as everyone always said he was.

The lawyers of Grant, Ronson & Greene are back for another season of scandals, secrets, and stilettos. As new allegiances form, friendships are tested and a shocking revelation threatens the very existence of the firm.

The Remarried Princess (Hulu & Disney+) - Nov. 4

Based on the hit Naver Webtoon of the same name, The Remarried Empress follows the strained relationship of beloved Empress Navier and her husband Emperor Sovieshu of the Eastern Kingdom. With anxieties rising across the kingdom, the couple’s relationship begins to fracture when Sovieshu falls in love with a runaway slave and attempts to move heaven and earth to win her heart. Unwilling to compromise her dignity, Navier acquiesces to the emperor’s requests on one condition – that she be allowed to remarry rival Crown Prince Heinrey of the Western Kingdom. What follows is a tale of love, lust and regret that threatens the fate of an entire kingdom as Navier strives to reclaim her power.

The documentary traces Muhammad Ali’s coming of age story, following a young Cassius Clay through the personal, professional and political battles he fought inside and outside the ring. Set against a changing America, The Greatest follows a once-in-a-generation talent fighting for the right to become his own man. Through the fights that made him a champion and the convictions that made him an icon, a young man from Louisville transforms himself into Muhammad Ali, the greatest of all time.

Taken: Natalee Holloway (Netflix) - Nov. 4

On May 30, 2005, 18-year-old Natalee Holloway vanished on a high school graduation trip to Aruba—and never came home. What followed was years of unanswered questions, a missing teenager, and a mother's relentless fight for the truth. Now, over 20 years later, Natalee's mother, Beth, is ready to tell the complete story. With exclusive, unprecedented access to Beth and those who were with Natalee when she vanished, this three-part documentary series is the definitive account of a case that gripped a nation and never let go. It's a story of a mother who refused to stop searching, an investigation that spanned continents, and a daughter whose memory endures. This is Natalee's story, told at last in full.

Helen (Keira Knightley) is still betraying her nation’s secrets to the covert organization she serves: the Black Doves. But after the misadventures of last Christmas, and with her husband Wallace (Andrew Buchan), preparing to become Prime Minister, she is walking a more treacherous line than ever.

Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook (Apple TV) - Nov. 6

The eight-episode series follows Nora Lum, aka Awkwafina, on a cross-country culinary road trip as she attempts to revive her family’s beloved Chinese restaurant.

Wolves Up Close With Bertie Gregory (National Geographic) - Nov. 6

Reconnecting with a pack of wolves he has followed for seven years, Bertie Gregory sets out to capture one of the Arctic’s most dangerous and rarely filmed hunts: wolves taking on a bull moose, prey roughly ten times their size. Led by Kona, a striking white breeding male, the pack faces a critical winter as dwindling food supplies, an encroaching rival wolf and an aging leader threaten its survival.

Charmed By a Southern Monster (Peacock) - Nov. 9

Starring Craig Conover as Hunter Caldwell and Nicole Mattox as Maeve Marchant, the series blends soapy romance, workplace rivalry and small-town mystery.

The story follows Maeve, a brilliant corporate fixer sent to convince and seduce Hunter, a rumored murderer, into selling his family’s estate. But when she discovers that the town’s most feared man may actually be its most misunderstood, and the only person who can protect her from her dangerous ex-boyfriend, Maeve becomes entangled in Hunter’s world. As family secrets and a billion-dollar development deal threaten to unravel their growing connection, she must confront her past and decide how much she’s willing to risk for love.

Whitney Way Thore is stepping into a transformative new chapter. Back in her home state of North Carolina, Whitney has found love with Jake, a man she first met years ago before reconnecting after her return to Charlotte. As their relationship deepens, Whitney is rediscovering her confidence through dance, exploring new possibilities on her health journey, and taking meaningful steps toward the future she’s always wanted, including her biggest dream of becoming a mom.

Picking up after the gut-wrenching mid-series finale, Tony Baddingham and Declan O'Hara's battle for the Cotswolds crown reaches fever pitch, while Rupert Campbell-Black is forced to confront his own personal demons. Against a backdrop of hedonistic parties, Bonfire Night chaos, the Hampshire Hunt Ball and a turbulent Christmas, affairs unravel, alliances fracture and rivalries intensify. Caught in the middle of the frenzied franchise war, Taggie O'Hara must find the courage to follow her heart, while those around her face the consequences of ambition, power and secrets that can no longer remain hidden. But as series two draws to a close, who will get their happy ending?

From Ron Howard, the documentary explores the life, career, and cultural impact of legendary American photographer Richard Avedon.

The Good Daughter is a suspenseful thriller wrapped in a deeply emotional story about love, family and resilience. Sisters Charlotte (Meghann Fahy) and Samantha (Rose Byrne) Quinn have spent the last 20 years trying to piece together the lives that were fractured by a single night of violence. When another attack splinters the small town of Pikeville, Charlotte – now a lawyer like her father – is the first witness on the scene. As the case unfolds and twists through painful memories and buried secrets, what emerges is not just a story of survival, but of enduring ties between a father and his daughters, and the complex bond between sisters.

After a reunion where the status of friendships and situationships remained ambiguous, the Charmers are determined to define their relationships and mend wounds. However, when true feelings bubble up and juicy rumors catch fire, the group seeks to unveil the truth – even if it costs them more than just friendships.

Three years into their jobs as response officers, Constables Grace Ellis, Tommy Foster, and Annie Conlon are operating at their limit, facing a new threat on the streets that the police can barely control. Meanwhile the murder trial of Gerry Cliff exposes a dangerous and long-buried secret that leads to chaos both inside the police, and across the criminal underworld. As they grapple with big decisions about their future, Grace, Tommy and Annie must find the courage to face the greatest threat they have ever encountered: the truth.

Each episode of the drama unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist, and the 12 days following the heist. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) who play a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the center of it all is the daring, epic raid on a bank vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich.

Expedition: Saving Our Seas (National Geographic) - Nov. 13

The documentary follows teams of National Geographic Explorers as they investigate our global Ocean, from seashore to seafloor and pole to pole. Combining cutting-edge technology with the knowledge of coastal communities, they chase the discoveries and solutions needed to protect our Oceans at a critical moment.

Homicide for the Holidays (Oxygen) - Nov. 14

The holidays are supposed to be the most wonderful time of the year. But for some families, cherished celebrations become the backdrop for unimaginable violence. Season six of Homicide For The Holidays brings a new batch of deadly deeds to the supposed jolliest time of the year as investigators pursue those responsible and seek justice for families shattered at a time meant for togetherness.

Diane Morgan returns as Philomena Cunk in a new series from Charlie Brooker. Billed as Cunk's most glamorous outing yet, she charts the history of cinema, from the invention of the camera and the New Wave filmmakers of the 1960s right up to the entrance of CGI and what the future of AI holds. Cunk will attempt to demystify it all while sitting in lumpy seats with stale popcorn, asking herself where did cinema come from? And why? What does it want? And why can’t it tell us?

Small Town Trouble: Texas (Bravo) - Nov. 18

Set in Boerne (pronounced "Bur-nee"), Texas, the series follows a charming yet unconventional group of wives, mothers and social insiders – Aaryn Williams, Alli McAnelly, Annari Uys, Gabby Hernandez Huffman, and Hailey Head, alongside their respective husbands – as conservative values of small-town life collide with forbidden attraction, messy friendships, and shocking   secrets. Here, perception is everything, temptation is everywhere, and the truth is never as buttoned-up as it looks.

The story of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye - before they were accused of stealing $8 billion and became Gen Z's own Bonnie & Clyde.

Nelly and Ashanti: We Belong Together (Peacock) - Nov. 19

This season, Ashanti continues to balance motherhood, continuing to perform on stage, and taking control of her musical legacy. While navigating living in St. Louis and New York City, Ashanti also juggles re-recording her debut album to retain her masters, finding time for her girlfriends who keep her grounded, and recording new music with some of music's hottest artists. After years of nonstop touring, Nelly reflects on the physical toll it’s taking at this stage in his life, and an unexpected family loss reminds him what matters most. Between raising their son, honoring their village, and planning for their future, Nelly and Ashanti discover that belonging together isn’t about standing still; it’s about building a future on their own terms.

Nearly a decade after a mysterious female jogger dubbed “The Mad Pooper” captured national attention for repeatedly defecating on residential lawns across Colorado Springs, one of the strangest unsolved mysteries is back in the spotlight. In the new two-hour special, viewers will dive headfirst into the bizarre true story that left an entire community searching for answers and asking one simple question: why?

As the survivors race to bury their sins before rescue arrives and an old flame roars back into town with plans of her own, turns out not every homecoming is a joyous one, and this one's going to sting.

Adapted from Tom Bradby's bestselling novel, Secret Service follows senior MI6 officer Kate Henderson (Gemma Arterton), whose covert investigation uncovers evidence that a high-ranking U.K. politician may be working as a Russian asset. With trust shattered and her career on the line, Kate must navigate the shifting sands of political loyalty, international threat, and personal sacrifice as she races to uncover their identity before it's too late.

The new comedy follows a team of dedicated archaeologists (and less-dedicated college students) who spend their summer working on a dig site in Greece. Their discovery of a rare artifact sends them on the adventure of a lifetime.

#840. Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax

John Aloisi’s players need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliff

With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic.

The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points.

They had been punished as part of a “special campaign to crack down on match-fixing, gambling and corruption in the football industry”, said a joint statement from the Chinese Football Association, the Ministry of Public Security and the General Administration of Sport at the time.

Chengdu were one of the seven to start on zero, above the defending champions Shanghai Port, who lost five points, and the runners-up Shanghai Shenhua who were hit with 10. It robbed the usual favourites of energy and it was all a bit surreal.

It almost felt over as soon as it started with Chengdu opening up a big lead, dropping just two points from the first 12 games while the usual powers struggled to get going.

Chengdu is a major city known more for its fiery Sichuan cuisine, genteel temples and cute pandas than football, despite English attempts to change that. In 2006, Sheffield United bought a local club but the Chengdu Blades were eventually dissolved in 2015. Four years later, City Football Group bought a stake in Sichuan Jiuniu but then moved the club to the southern city of Shenzhen in 2024.

Chengdu Rongcheng were formed in 2018, coming up through the divisions to finally, this season, be within touching distance of the championship. But just two wins from the past 13 and three defeats in a row mean the leaders are not limping to the line but have collapsed right next to it.

It should have been over weeks ago. On 10 October, more than 40,000 fans were ready to celebrate the title but an added‑time goal from Alberto Quiles gave Tianjin Jinmen Tiger a 1-0 win and postponed the celebrations. Next up was a trip to Shanghai Port but that ended in a 3-0 defeat. The penultimate game of the season came against challengers Dalian Yingbo, when again, just avoiding defeat was needed. It was another painful experience as they lost 1-0 after missing a first-half penalty and having a 90th-minute equaliser ruled out by the video assistant referee.

Chengdu have not scored in almost seven hours of football while Dalian are the form team with four consecutive wins. If they win a fifth against Tianjin then Chengdu need a point at fourth‑placed Shandong Taishan as the league is decided by head-to-head results before goal difference. Not many think they will. Even fewer hope so. Dalian and the 60,000 fans who attend home games are the people’s choice. Chengdu are not popular because their fans have developed a poor reputation. Last November, the club were fined about $70,000 (£52,200) after some home supporters racially abused Henan FC’s Ghanaian striker Frank Acheampong, just weeks after a punishment of $3,000 after travelling supporters at a Champions League game in South Korea threw bottles at the Ulsan HD players.

Whatever happens it is an unexpected and dramatic ending to a season that started in shock and the usual negative international headlines that surround Chinese football. The grandstand finish is welcome and average attendances have risen. They are poised to finish at about 30,000, a considerable jump from 25,755 last season and, by some distance, the best in Asia. Regional leagues have been enjoying some popularity too, showing that there is genuine love for the game in the country; a passion that grows better when it is organic from the bottom rather than organised from the top.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

The national side is still a problem, though, and even for a fanbase well accustomed to disappointment the recent 5-0 defeat against Palestine at home, the fourth-biggest loss in history, was tough to take. As one journalist said, being thrashed by Brazil, Japan and Wales is one thing, but Palestine was another. There were some mitigating circumstances in that a number of national team players were at the Asian Games, where China actually performed well, losing narrowly against South Korea in the bronze final.

There are signs that the gap behind Korea is not as wide as it used to be. China reached the final of the under-17 and under-23 Asian championships this year before losing both against Japan. Compared with the rest of Asia’s best, young Chinese players are closing the gap at a technical and tactical level. Exporting more players to Europe is necessary to play at a higher level and if that happens, that senior national shirt may feel a little lighter.

Failure can, however, be hard to shake off as Chengdu Rongcheng may well find out if they mess this up.

#838. Why Matthew Stafford’s Wife Kelly Stafford Is Calling Out the NFL

Kelly Stafford, wife of Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, questioned the NFL's decision to schedule the Los Angeles team's bye week with only 10 days off, rather than the usual 11 to 14.

Kelly Stafford is throwing a flag on the NFL's schedule.

As the Los Angeles Rams continue to hit the field during the 2026 season, quarterback Matthew Stafford's wife sent a pointed message to the league about the team's calendar.

"Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week," Kelly wrote on her Instagram Stories Nov. 3. "Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap."

The registered nurse—who shares 9-year-old twin girls Sawyer and Chandler, as well as daughters Hunter, 8, and Tyler, 6, with Matthew—may not be lacing up her cleats, but she knows when a time-out may be needed.

"I'm tired just watching from the stands," she continued. "Can't imagine how the guys feel."

Although teams generally have their bye weeks after a Sunday game and don't play again for 11 to 14 days, both the Rams and Green Bay Packers—who face off on the day before Thanksgiving (Nov. 25)—will return to the field after 10 days.

Other teams with a bye week at the same time, including the Cleveland Browns, New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks, will still take a full 14 days off.

E! News has reached out to the NFL for comment and has not yet heard back.

Not every schedule may be a touchdown, but the league does try its best to ensure each team has a restful week off, which is determined by the number of cross-country games scheduled, stadium conflicts and other operational obstacles.

"The scheduling teams aim to balance these operational elements while still trying to maximize fan viewership," the NFL Operations website explained. "The process is challenging, and there may be no such thing as a perfect schedule, but the schedule makers consistently try to provide the NFL's fans and broadcast partners with a compelling and entertaining slate of games week after week."

While Kelly is willing to call a foul on the Rams' calendar, she will always cheer on her husband, who has been her MVP since they married in 2015.

"He is the softest, most patient man," she told E! News in 2022. "My dad always said one of the most important relationships in life is a father-daughter relationship just because of the confidence your dad can give you."

"I am so grateful that I ended up with Matthew," she added, "because he sets such an incredible example as to the partner they should want to be with."

As the Staffords prepare for another week of football, keep reading for a closer look at their game-winning family moments.

On the field, Matthew Stafford is one of the best quarterbacks of the NFL. But when the football player comes home, he's simply dad.

During bye-week, Matthew and his wife Kelly Stafford treated their kids to a festive fall day near their home in Los Angeles.

"33 and grateful for the people that fill this home," Kelly wrote when celebrating her birthday. "Thankful for these girls' contagious smiles and for a husband who never fails to make me laugh."

"A pier breakfast, turned beach day, turned watching pro female surfing competition…" Kelly wrote on Instagram. "Pretty epic summer day with great 'aloha vibes.'"

After playing at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, Matthew was able to reunite with three of his daughters in a suite.

After cheering for Dad all day long, it's no surprise that Matthew's kids just want to snuggle after game day.

Whether they are at the stadium or going to school, Matthew's daughters love to wear the Rams' team colors.

When Matthew worked from home during COVID-19 shutdowns, his daughters quickly wore him out.

"My whole heart in one photo," Kelly wrote on Instagram when capturing her daughters snuggling by Matthew.

#837. Azeez to Andrés: seven smart-looking Premier League deadline day deals

An 18-year-old who has played at two major international tournaments and the division’s top clearance maker from last season also feature

A tricky, exciting, quick and versatile midfielder, Azeez has proven himself in the Championship with Millwall over the past two seasons and now deserves a chance to test himself in the top flight.

Brighton had been chasing him for a while and struck a deal on deadline day for a very reasonable reported initial £12.5m, rising to £15m. If he can make the step up and produce anything like his second-tier form, he’ll be a steal.

He is a high-volume producer at the sharp end of the pitch, constantly making things happen that threaten the opposition’s goal, but standing out most for his crossing. He ranked top of the Championship last season for open-play crosses (227) and expected assists from crosses (6.71 xA).

He also ranked fourth for dribble attempts (131), ninth for shots (95), sixth for chances created from open play (58). He created good-quality chances, too; only two players created more big chances than he did (18), and he ranked fourth for expected assists. His 9.12 xA alongside only seven assists suggests he may benefit from playing alongside better finishers.

A hugely exciting prospect. Despite being 18, Mbaye has significant and noteworthy experience under his belt. Last year he made six appearances, including in the final, for Senegal at the Africa Cup of Nations and this summer he made four appearances at the World Cup. He has also played in two Ligue 1 title-winning campaigns, including 2024-25, when he became the youngest player in PSG’s history to start a game, and won the Champions League in both of those seasons

He is a dribbling and ball-carrying menace, who always looks as if he’s about to do something special. Among players to play at least 900 minutes in Ligue 1 last season, he was 11th for carries (moving at least five metres with the ball) per 90, with 20.0, and 12th for progressive carries (moving at least five metres upfield with the ball) per 90, with 10.3. Most of the players above him in both lists are defenders, who naturally have more space to move into.

He was third for take-on-ending carries, or running with the ball for at least five metres before attempting to beat an opponent with a dribble, with 2.9 per 90. And he also has end product to boot. He scored at Afcon and the World Cup despite limited minutes and his 0.45 goals or assists per 90 for PSG last season is not to be sniffed at.

Danso had a pretty impossible task over his two years at Tottenham. He was the back-up to the first-choice centre-backs Cristian Romero and Micky van de Ven, playing intermittently on both sides of central defence in dysfunctional teams jumping between styles of play, and he very rarely played for any consistent run of games.

He was unfairly compared with the players he was replacing for much of his time there, but the truth is he was always reliable enough. He excelled, however, when Romero got injured during the run-in last season and he was called upon in Spurs’ time of need as they scraped clear of relegation.

He may not be the best on the ball – though he is hardly terrible – but he is an excellent deep defender. Among those to play at least 1,000 minutes in the Premier League last season, Danso ranked first for clearances (8.2 per 90) and headed clearances (6.3), and was fifth for aerial duels won (4.8 per 90).

He could thrive at Sunderland, who spent more of their out-of-possession game time in a low block than any other team in the Premier League last season (25%). Danso could be perfectly at home in this setup, paired alongside the player he beat into second place for clearances and headed clearances: Dan Ballard.

It was always said during Pep Guardiola’s time at Manchester City that attackers had their wings clipped in terms of individual freedom, limited to playing within the parameters of the manager’s meticulous gameplan.

But dribbling ability became increasingly important in the final years of his reign, with Jérémy Doku and Antoine Semenyo on the wings and Rayan Cherki in between. Doku (162) and Semenyo (144) ranked first and second for dribbles attempted in the Premier League last season, with Cherki ninth (111). They also ranked first (84), fourth (59) and eighth (51), respectively, for dribbles completed.

With the deadline-day addition of Ndiaye, City have gone in even harder on dribbling ability under Enzo Maresca. The Senegal international ranked second for dribbles attempted (136) and dribbles completed (73) in the Premier League last season.

Fernandez-Pardo’s versatility is a major attraction. He’s comfortable playing off the left and cutting in on to his right foot, or as a No 9. Although not the bulkiest, he has explosive pace and promises to be a threat in behind.

The Belgium international is arguably at his most threatening when running with the ball because he does so with such purpose. His 122 carries progressing the ball at least 10 metres upfield in Ligue 1 last term were bettered by only seven players, several of whom were defenders.

On top of that, he ranked top for carries into the penalty area (69) and seventh for carries ending with a shot or chance created (39).

Fofana appeared to be enjoying a swift rise in 2024-25, only for a serious ankle injury to massively disrupt his development in 2025-26. Sunderland will be hoping they can get him back to the levels shown the season before last, when he was a real livewire on Lyon’s left flank.

He contributed nine goal involvements (five goals, four assists) in 1,586 minutes in Ligue 1 in 2024-25, averaging one every 176 minutes. Only eight forwards (900+ mins) averaged more expected assists per 90 (0.25).

The most eye-catching aspects of his game, however, were his dynamism and pace. He could be difficult to stop once moving, and this made him a very useful outlet. Among Ligue 1 forwards (900+ mins), his 16.6 carries per 90 ranked him sixth, and he moved up to third for progressive carries per 90 (11.5).

Fofana is direct, exciting and has significant potential. He is a player Sunderland could make a profit on if he reaches the levels previously expected.

Andrés arrived to bolster Brighton’s midfield options after Carlos Baleba’s exit to Manchester United. Although a different type of midfielder to the Cameroonian, Chema is another with vast potential.

A product of Real Madrid’s academy, Chema joined Stuttgart last summer. During his sole campaign in the Bundesliga, he was in and out of the team but caught the eye at the base of their midfield.

Comparisons have been made to Rodri because of his physical attributes and nominal role as a holding midfielder. He doesn’t have anything like the same influence in possession but Chema is tidy on the ball.

It’s what he offers defensively that is most notable, however. He’s been broadly praised for his anticipation and reading of the game, ranking second among midfielders (900+ mins) since the start of last season for interceptions per 90 in the Bundesliga (2.3).

The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer

Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. Avoiding a repeat of last year’s upheaval was a major boost. Keith Andrews held on to his best players and made smart additions to a solid squad. Mamadou Sangaré has added quality in midfield since joining from Lens and looks the bargain of the summer. Callum Wilson has brought experience up front after signing on a free and Jaidon Anthony provides cover on the flanks after his £15m move from Burnley. El Hadji-Malick Diouf, signed from West Ham, offers potential at left-back. Jacob Steinberg

Deadline day deals to bring in the exciting Nigeria forward Femi Azeez from Millwall and the Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés from Stuttgart made it 12 signings in another summer of transition, Azeez’s arrival being announced almost 12 hours after the window shut. The departures of Jan Paul van Hecke, Carlos Baleba and Carl Rushworth brought in more than £140m as the Brighton model continues to deliver big profits, although losing last season’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, to Chelsea for a mere £5m may be the biggest loss if the new striker Promise David cannot bring the goals. #835. Taylor Swift Shook Off One Concern Before Saying Yes to Toy Story 5

Before Taylor Swift agreed to write the end credits song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for Toy Story 5, she said she confirmed no one else would be kicked off the project in order for her to do it.

However, the Grammy winner recently shared that before she agreed to saddle up and write the original song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for Toy Story 5, she had to make sure no one else would get booted from the project.

That’s because Swift was initially approached about writing the end credits song while she was on her record-breaking Eras Tour, but she put off taking the meeting until months after it ended so that she could rest.

“I was repeatedly asking, ‘I know that it took me a couple months to come back to this project. Be honest: did you guys replace me?’” the 36-year-old recalled of the meeting during a Nov. 1 Q&A. “‘I don't want to kick somebody off of this project that you reached out to after [me] because I understand, but I'm not in the business of doing that.’”

But the “Cardigan” singer soon realized she was patient zero.

“I found out that there was no other person on your mood board,” she said alongside director Andrew Stanton during the joint Q&A. “Everybody said, ‘No, we just decided there wasn't going to be an end credit song [if you didn’t do it].’”

So, Swift went to infinity and beyond to make sure she and her cowriter Jack Antonoff captured the Pixar film’s story.

“When I saw this brilliant film that Andrew made, I realized exactly why he knew I would love it,” she explained. “It's centered around Jesse, who's my favorite character, and it deals with female friendship.”

And as Swift put it, “It's crazy how I could see a way into all the characters in a way, and it was like a struck-by-lightning moment of like, ‘I have to go home, get to my piano, and write this song, because I know exactly what I would want to say if I had you know the privilege of writing for this.’”

To learn about the inspiration behind some of Swift’s other iconic tracks, keep reading…

Before The Life of a Showgirl, the only track Taylor had certainly written about her guy on the Chiefs—save for The Eras Tour “Karma” rewrite, of course—is “So High School,” which the now-engaged couple aptly set their proposal Instagram post to in August 2025.

Although some fans speculate “The Alchemy,” also off The Tortured Poets Department, is about Travis for the football and high school metaphors sprinkled in the track, “So High School” includes a more obvious nod with the lyrics: “Are you going to marry, kiss or kill me? / It’s just a game but really / I’m betting on all three, for us two.”

Indeed, Travis revealed to AfterBuzzTV back in 2016 that “Taylor Swift, would be the kiss,” in a game of “Marry, Kiss, Kill” between her, Ariana Grande and Katy Perry.

As for how Travis feels about the track? Although it’s a tough competition as a Swiftie, it’s his all-time favorite.

“I’m not gonna lie,” he joked of the choice to Access Hollywood in 2024. “I might be a little biased.”

But now that Taylor has found the guy who can call her honey, he's the one she most wants to pay tribute to in verse.

On The Life of a Showgirl, she sang about her now-husband topping her "Wi$h Li$t," serving as her "forever night stand" in "Honey," and turning her sky "Opalite."

And, forgive her, it sounds cocky, but in "Wood," her raciest song yet, she shared how Travis' love was the key that opened her thighs.

Fortunately, Taylor's mom Andrea Swift, "thinks that the song is about superstitions, which it absolutely is," Taylor joked on SiriusXM’s Morning Mash Up after the album's October 2025 release. "That’s the joy of the double entendre. You can read that song for people, and it just goes right over their heads."

But it wasn't hard to grasp who she was calling "the love of my life" on the Encore track "Cleveland!," the title itself an overt nod to Travis' hometown.

Although short-lived, Taylor appeared to write several songs on The Tortured Poets Department about her dalliance with The 1975 frontman in 2023, including the album’s title track which also name drops their mutual pal and collaborator Jack Antonoff.

Other tracks rumored to be about Matty include “Fortnight,” “Down Bad,” and “But Daddy I Love Him,” the latter of which also appears to call out the backlash Taylor received for her relationship with him.

And while Matty told paparazzi, per Entertainment Tonight in 2024 that he hadn’t listened to the album, though he was "sure it’s good," his mother Denise Welch slammed his alleged connection to the breakup ballads.

"You're not allowed to say anything," the Loose Woman cohost said during a 2025 appearance on Watch What Happens Live, "and then she writes a whole album about it."

For more on Matty’s place in Taylor’s catalogue, read here.

It's actually sweet all the time an unnamed rival has spent on the singer. Or, at least, that's what Taylor conveyed in The Life of a Showgirl track "Actually Romantic."

Rather than share her praise for Travis or even an ex-lover, the musician actually sings about a person who "high-fived my ex and then you said you're glad he ghosted me. Wrote me a song saying it makes you sick to see my face / Some people might be offended / But it's actually sweet."

Fans were quick to say the clues pointed toward Charli XCX, who opened for Taylor on her Reputation Tour and is close with Taylor's ex Matty and his now-wife Gabbriette Bechtel.

Another tell was Charli's 2024 brat track "Sympathy Is a Knife," in which the British musician—married to Matty's The 1975 bandmate George Daniel—sings, "Don’t wanna see her backstage at my boyfriend’s show. Fingers crossed behind my back / I hope they break up real quick."

Good thing for Brittany Mahomes, Taylor likes her friends canceled. Because fans feel the singer was thinking of the former soccer player—wed to Travis' teammate Patrick Mahomes—or onetime BFF Blake Lively when she wrote about standing by a pal's side when the whole world has seemingly turned on them.

But really the person at the crux of The Life of a Showgirl track is Taylor herself, who felt her reputation took several hits after her very public 2016 feud with Kanye West and then-wife Kim Kardashian.

"Having had my own experiences with mass judgment and being at the center of many dramatic, scandalous moments in my career, where people were all weighing in at once or at least it felt like that," she told Amazon Music, "having had those experiences, it makes me move through the world a little bit differently."

And now she wants to gift that what-doesn't-kill-you-makes-you-stronger mentality to others. As the lyrics suggest, Taylor continued, "I don't just naturally cast people aside just because other people decide they don't like them. I make my own decisions about people based on how they treat me within my life and their actions."

Amid their six-year relationship, Taylor penned several songs about—and with—the Conversations With Friends star. Shortly after the pair's relationship was confirmed in 2016, she released Reputation, which included several songs presumably about Joe such as “Call It What You Want,” “Dress,” and “King of My Heart.”

On Lover, Taylor also included the track "Cornelia Street," a nod to the New York City rental she was living in during the early months of their romance. Elsewhere in her discography, fans believe Taylor also penned "invisible string," on folklore about her romance with Joe, as well as Midnights' "Sweet Nothing" and its bonus track 'You’re Losing Me," which her producer Jack confirmed was written two years before Taylor's 2023 breakup with Joe.

Joe is one of the many people in Taylor’s life who has also become her cowriter on songs, earning credits on folklore and evermore songs like "betty," "champagne problems," "exile" and others under the pseudonym William Bowery.

"It was really the most accidental thing to happen in lockdown," the Brutalist alum told GQ of the cowriting credits in 2022. "It was just messing around on a piano and singing badly and being overheard and then thinking, you know, what if we tried to get to the end of it together?"

For more songs inspired by Joe, see here.

Following the infamous—and later revealed to be edited—phone call leak in 2016 between Kanye and Taylor over a reference he made to her on his The Life of Pablo album, Taylor has subtly clapped back at the divorced couple more than once.

As recently as 2024, Taylor penned "thanK you aIMee" likely about Kim, given she capitalized letters in the track's title to spell out her name. (In another variant of the TTPD album, she changed the letters to capitalize "YE" in the track, as an apparent nod toward the rapper.)

Prior to TTPD, Taylor also sprinkled hits against Kim and Kanye for the "Famous" feud, with "Mad Woman," on folklore, where she sings, "Women like hunting witches too / Doing your dirtiest work for you / It’s obvious that wanting me dead has really brought you two together."

Taylor’s first Reputation single "Look What You Made Me Do," was also a nod to the public fallout, as well as "This Is Why We Can’t Have Nice Things," in which she sings about a once-repaired friendship fracturing again.

But, of course, Taylor's musical inspirations from Kanye date back to that 2009 MTV VMA incident, when he interrupted her speech for Best Female Video at the Video Music Awards. In Speak Now’s "Innocent," she forgives Kanye for the viral moment, which earned him backlash from figures as prominent as then-president Barack Obama.

"It's OK / Life is a tough crowd," Taylor sings on the track, going on to reference his age at the time of the VMAs. "32 and still growing up now / Who you are is not what you did / You’re still an innocent."

For a thorough dive into Taylor’s beef with Kanye, see here.

Taylor and the Loki actor may have only had a short-lived romance in the summer of 2016, but it did inspire more than one track for the "Karma" singer. Indeed, many fans speculated that "Getaway Car," and "High Infidelity" are about the timeline of their romance in comparison to her relationship with Calvin Harris. She and the DJ split in June 2016 after one year of dating, the same month she sparked rumors with Tom.

In both songs, Taylor sings about how a relationship born out of slight infidelity is doomed from the start.

While fans are sure these three are the ones who made up the "Getaway Car" sideshow, neither Taylor, nor Calvin or Tom have addressed the inspiration for the songs.

Although Taylor shut down any speculation that she wrote songs about her romance with the One Direction alum, there are a lot of subtle references to the "Watermelon Sugar" singer on 1989.

"Style," is the most obvious nod to Harry, simply for the title, as well as "Out of the Woods," and bonus track "Wonderland," which references a "Cheshire cat smile"—which many fans see as a nod to Harry’s hometown of Holmes Chapel in Cheshire, England.

Meanwhile, the 1989 vault track "Is It Over Now?" paints a vivid picture of the moment Taylor knew her romance with Harry was done for good.

"Blue dress on a boat," she sings in reference to the infamous January 2013 photo of her after the couple’s alleged breakup in the Virgin Islands. "Your new girl is my clone."

On "Now That We Don’t Talk," she references the doomed vacation again, and slams Harry’s infamous music taste in the lines, "I don’t have to pretend I like acid rock / Or that I’d like to be on a mega-yacht."

And while Taylor went on to date several more stars from across the pond, Harry was her first British bloke. And since London is referenced in other songs in her earlier catalogue, including Red’s "Come Back, Be Here" and "Message in a Bottle," the tracks are also speculated to be about Harry.

Harry didn’t earn the entirety of 1989’s inspiration. Indeed, many fans believe the track "Bad Blood" is about Katy as Taylor teased to Rolling Stone in 2014 it was about another "female artist," who "tried to sabotage an entire arena tour."

"I was like, 'Oh, we’re just straight-up enemies,'" Taylor, who at the time saw some of her background dancers leave for Katy's Prismatic tour, added. "It wasn’t even about a guy! It had to do with business."

However, Taylor maintained she penned the song simply to get some feelings off her chest.

"My intent was not to create some gossip-fest," she added to Rolling Stone. "I wanted people to apply it to a situation where they felt betrayed in their own lives."

Ultimately, though, the song fueled a feud—with Katy posting on X one day after the Rolling Stone piece published, "Watch out for Regina George in sheep’s clothing."

The singers were later able to squash their beef in 2019, after which Katy made a cameo in Taylor’s "You Need to Calm Down" music video.

Taylor can write fanfiction, too. Ahead of the release of Red, Taylor met Ethel while dating her grandson Conor Kennedy, and ultimately penned the song "Starlight" about a reimagined version of a date night between the Kennedy matriarch and her late husband.

"Starlight is a song that I wrote after seeing a picture of Ethel and Bobby Kennedy when they were 17," Taylor explained in a Red interview. "I didn’t know anything about what they were doing or what was going on in the picture, but I just thought 'They look like they’re having the best night.' And so I wrote this song about what the night might’ve been like."

In response to the nod, Ethel told the Cape Cod Times, "She is just sensational, inside and out."

One of Taylor’s most popular breakup songs of all time "All Too Well"—and its 10-minute alternate version—is thought to be about the Donnie Darko star. After all, it references autumn—when their short-lived 2010 romance took place—her subject’s sister’s house, and a certain scarf. (Jake, of course, has a very famous sister in Maggie Gyllenhaal, and the duo passed a striped Gucci scarf between them during their romance.)

Taylor also appeared to take shots at her romance with Jake in "The Last Time," "We Are Never Getting Back Together," and the Red vault track "I Bet You Think About Me," which call out the subject’s music taste and wealthy background.

Despite widespread belief Red as a whole was mostly inspired by Jake, he shut down any connection following the album’s 2021 rerelease.

"It’s about her relationship with her fans," he told Esquire in 2022. "It is her expression."

Taylor, meanwhile, did concur with Jake's sentiment, noting that she saw "All Too Well" become something much deeper than a breakup song.

"What was so crazy is that when it went out into the world, the fans just among themselves decided it was their favorite too," she explained on Good Morning America in 2021.  "They just sort of ... claimed it as the most important song from Red...over the course of the first six months the album was out."

Many fans speculate that The Tortured Poets Department's "The Manuscript" is about the impact of "All Too Well," and thus, Taylor's relationship with Jake.

Yes, at least half of Taylor’s heart—at the age of 19, anyway—once belonged to the "Gravity" musician. And it possibly led to some of her Speak Now tracks like "Dear John," and "The Story of Us," which Taylor previously revealed were inspired by the same person.

"'The Story of Us' is about running into someone I had been in a relationship with at an awards show, and we were seated a few seats away from each other," she told USA Today in 2010. "I just wanted to say to him, 'Is this killing you? Because it's killing me.' But I didn't. Because I couldn't. Because we both had these silent shields up."

While Taylor has said she doesn’t use Easter eggs to hint at her personal life, the "Story of Us" liner notes—where Taylor used to hide messages for her fans—on the original Speak Now album spelled out "CMT Awards," an event she and John both attended in 2010.

As for where "Dear John" is concerned? John himself had to respond to the brazen shots fired.

"I didn’t deserve it," the musician told Rolling Stone in 2012. "I'm pretty good at taking accountability now, and I never did anything to deserve that. It was a really lousy thing for her to do."

Once too young to be messed with, Taylor is now too wise to be bothered with any drama. "I don’t care about anything that happened to me when I was 19," she told fans ahead of playing "Dear John," at The Eras Tour in 2023. "Except for the songs that I wrote and the memories we made together."

As she put it, “I do not care. We’ve all grown up. We’re good.”

Following a 2009 romance with the Twilight star, Taylor penned "Back to December" about the relationship. In addition to alluding to a "September night" where her subject saw her cry (Lautner was also at the 2009 VMAs), she included a nod to him in the song’s liner notes, which read, "Tay."

Ahead of Speak Now's rerelease in 2023, the Sharkboy and Lava Girl alum joked about his role in the album’s songs, telling Today at the time, "I feel safe."

Some fans also speculate that "Today Was a Fairytale" and "I Can See You"—the music video he starred in—were about her Valentine’s Day costar as well, as in the latter track, Taylor sings about keeping "everything professional," before a romance ensued.

Believe it or not, Taylor once got butterflies from the "Fireflies" singer. "Enchanted" is about a night she met the frontman for Owl City, and she revealed she included the line "wonderstruck" so he’d know it was about him, as he had used the word in an email to her.

"Meeting him," Taylor told Yahoo in 2010. "It was this overwhelming feeling of: I really hope that you’re not in love with somebody."

A year later, Adam responded to the musical love letter by rerecording the song, adding in his own lyrics, "Oh Taylor, I was so enchanted to meet you too."

"I'll be the first to admit I’m a rather shy boy and since music is the most eloquent form of communication I can muster, I decided to record something for you–a sort of a 'reply' to the breathtaking song on your current record," he added in a note beneath the song, shared to his band's website at the time. "You are a true princess from a dreamy fairy tale."

Once upon a time, Taylor was extremely up front when it came to who inspired her songs, especially where her breakup with Joe Jonas is concerned. Back in 2008, she quickly penned "Forever and Always" and tacked it on as a last-minute addition to Fearless, perfectly timed to her infamous appearance on Ellen, where she called out the Jonas Brothers member for breaking up with her in a 27-second phone call.

On her next album, Speak Now, released in 2010, Taylor included two nods to Joe, including "Last Kiss," a heart-wrenching ballad which references July 9, a.k.a. the date of the 2008 Jonas Brothers concert she attended while she and Joe were still together.

Elsewhere on the album, Taylor included "Better Than Revenge," which was a clap back at the Jonas Brothers’ song "Much Better," which had a not-so-veiled reference to her in the lyric, "I'm done with superstars and all the tears on her guitar."

Later on in her discography, Taylor included fonder nods to her past romance with Joe on Red’s "Holy Ground," and folklore’s "Invisible String," the latter in which she reflects on becoming friendly with him in more recent years. "Cold was the steel of my axe to grind for the boys who broke my heart," she sings in the song, "Now I send their babies presents."

However, when Taylor released Fearless (Taylor’s Version) in 2021, she gave Joe one more whack with "Mr. Perfectly Fine," though she penned the song around the time of their 2008 breakup. It was Joe’s now-ex-wife Sophie Turner who seemingly confirmed the track was about her then-husband, sharing the song to social media at the time and joking, "It's not NOT a bop."
