#783. La La Anthony and Carmelo Anthony Settle Divorce 9 Years After Breakup

La La Anthony and Carmelo Anthony—parents to their 19-year-old son Kiyan Carmelo Anthony—finalized their divorce on Nov. 4, following 11 years of marriage.

No more balls in the air for La La Anthony and Carmelo Anthony.

The former couple—who were married for over a decade—settled their divorce five years after the Power actress filed to end the marriage in 2021 due to irreconcilable differences from the retired NBA all-star.

On Nov. 4, the Anthonys—who initially split in 2017 before briefly reconciling in 2018—were granted a certificate of dissolution after they each signed affidavits agreeing to the terms, according to court docs obtained by E! News.

And while sorting out child support became a non-issue as their 19-year-old son, Kiyan Carmelo Anthony, turned 18 before the divorce was finalized, a "qualified medical child support order" is still listed as pending on the docs. This order typically mandates that a child will be enrolled in a parent's health care plan.

The divorce settlement marks the conclusion to the romance, which began in 2003 when Carmelo asked mutual friend DJ Clue to introduce him to the MTV personality. (In 2017, the former New York Knick welcomed daughter Genesis Harlo Anthony with ex Mia Angel Burks during his initial split from La La.)

And while the Brooklyn hometown heroes have sidelined their marriage for good, La La previously looked back on how she believes public scrutiny contributed to their breakup, calling the pressure of the spotlight "really hard."

"When we lived here [in New York] under all of that, that's when things became complicated," she shared on Call Her Daddy in 2022. "Now that I look back, that was kind of the start of the demise of the marriage."

Still, in this new era of their relationship—Carmelo is dating model Racquel Smith, meanwhile La La has been romantically linked to Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and entrepreneur Bear Da Prince—both parents remain focused on co-parenting.

"At the end of the day, the center of everything is Kiyan," La La told E! News in 2023. "We want to show Kiyan that his parents love each other and we're a family. We want to be good representations of that to Kiyan."

Want to know ball on which NBA couples are still together? Don't dribble away...

All Jordyn Woods wanted for Christmas in 2025 was Karl-Anthony Towns' rooftop proposal. "Marry Christmas," the model captioned her Dec. 25 Instagram post, showing the New York Knicks center taking a knee at NYC's Overstory.

And while the massive rectangular sparkler she's been sporting since 2024 was quite the winning play, simply having fun together are the true Xs and Os to their romance. "I think it's kind of cool dating your best friend," she said on her Instagram series Regular-ish in 2021. "We know each other. We know each other's hearts. We know each other on good days and bad days and we've been through a lot of bad days together."

Of course, Aug. 15, 2026 was one of the best yet, the pair marrying in front of their squad in Malibu.

Just because singer Coco Jones wasn't ready to open up her romantic playbook doesn't mean she was hiding her years-long romance with Cleveland Cavaliers shooting guard Donovan Mitchell. "Secrecy is not what I prefer," the "ICU" musician explained during a March 2025 appearance on Club Shay Shay. "I don’t want to feel like I have to be somebody secret. I don’t want to make anybody feel like they’re mine."

Instead, added the Bel-Air actress, "For me, I'm trying to protect myself, and I’m trying to protect my family and who I love, so I am more private."

But the truth is, maybe she, she, she, she, she needs the seven-time NBA All-Star, who shared drone footage of his oceanside proposal in July 2025. Diving into her bridal era, "It's unexplainable," she told E! News at the 2026 Grammys. "I'm like, 'Wow, I've been to so many events, I've planned so many things, I've been to so many fittings, I've worn so many amazing things, but this is unexplainable.'"

Her hard work netted a dream wedding when they wed in Connecticut on Aug. 1, 2026.

At Jayson Tatum's lowest point, it was his family that convinced him to keep shooting his shot. When the Boston Celtics' star forward ruptured his Achilles during the 2025 playoffs, "I could have been like, 'You know what, I'm done. I've accomplished enough,'' the 2024 champ admitted to E! News. "But I thought about the people I would be letting down."

That included sons Deuce (from a previous relationship) and Dylan, with singer girlfriend Ella Mai. "I thought about my kids," the six-time All-Star explained. "Use this opportunity to show them, 'This is what dad went through, and he had a choice to make. We always have choices to make in our lives. What choice are you going to make?'"

One key move that he and the "Boo’d Up" musician decided on is to not diagram their five-plus year relationship. "I think it’s been a weird topic because obviously I never announced it myself," she explained during a December 2025 episode of Capital XTRA. "So, people don’t know whether or not to say it. But I’m not going to act like I don’t have a child. I have a child."

A talented one, at that. "I try not to overdo it because I don’t want him to grow up and be like, 'She just pushed her music down my throat,'" she told E! of their 2024 arrival. "But I do try and play a lot of music around him."

When Philadelphia 76ers big man Joel Embiid was first introduced to future wife Anne de Palma at a 2018 dinner with a mutual friend, he avoided a full-court press. Instead, she told ESPN in 2021, "It started off as a beautiful friendship."

Both transplants to the U.S.—he left Cameroon as a teen to play basketball; the Brazilian model signed her first contract at age 14—they soon learned they each spoke French and shared a love of soccer. "We FaceTimed every day for a while," de Palma continued, but she soon realized he was her personal MVP. "He just has this personality where he wants to motivate you."

Three years after the SI Swimsuit fixture and the seven-time All-Star welcomed son Arthur (named for his younger brother, who died in a 2014 car crash) in September 2020, they wed in the Hamptons. "He pushes all of us to be the best of ourselves," de Palma raved to ESPN of the 76ers center. "That's the type of person you want to have around."

Las Vegas Aces standout A'ja Wilson isn't just an MVP to the WNBA, where she nabbed her league-leading fourth title in 2025. She also provides a crucial lift to boyfriend Bam Adebayo. When the Miami Heat's star center bested Kobe Bryant's record, scoring 83 points against the Washington Wizards on March 10, 2026, he credited his longtime teammate.

"To have 83 the first game she's here is very special," the three-time All-Star said in a video shared by the NBA on social media. "The behind-the-scenes, the workouts, the conversations, they're very motivating, and obviously you see what she does ... you get inspired by that. I'm thankful to have her in my life."

He provides quite the assist as well. When the University of South Carolina retired her jersey in 2025, Wilson shared, "I wouldn't be who I am today without the love, support and sacrifices of so many people. And what a blessing to have those most special to me courtside today, especially my favorite Olympian from out of town."

Still, there have been definitive clues that the Bayou Barbie has found her Ken in Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. "That’s a sign," the Atlanta Dream power forward captioned a TikTok showcasing an impressive arrangements of roses, "that’s a signnnn." And it was certainly a big play when the Duke alum turned up to the 2025 WNBA All-Star game sporting a t-shirt baring Reese's visage.

The NCAA champ—set to appear on season two of The Hunting Wives—returned the favor, attending a December 2025 Magic game in a jersey emblazoned with the words "My Man."

When it comes to planning her future wedding to Milwaukee Bucks power forward Kyle Kuzma, model Winnie Harlow is still studying that metaphorical game film. "At this point, we're trying to get to a point of where," she explained to E! News in September 2025, seven months after the NBA champ proposed during a Valentine's Day trip to Turks and Caicos, "and then we can get everything flowing."

A few keys to the game: "I'm an island vibe," explained the America's Next Top Model alum. "So, I really want to have warm weather, and I want to have a lot of dancing. I'm that type."

And no doubt Kuzma will dish out some key assists, having truly scored with his island engagement. "I never really asked her what type of ring she liked or anything," he told Vogue of dreaming up the 8.5-carat stunner. "I just wanted to draw a picture of what I felt resembled her—something that was elegant, but very timeless and simplistic at the same time."

Memphis native GloRilla left a Thanksgiving 2024 game between her hometown Grizzlies and the New Orleans Pelicans feeling quite grateful that their star forward Brandon Ingram made a move. "But that's it," the musician told Complex in 2025, "that's all I'm gonna say!"

But every now and then, she'll throw it down. As she wrote in a January 2026 Instagram post, "Might let him dunk dis like he dunk da balllll."

The true MVP of the household, Savannah Brinson was small forward LeBron James' teammate long before he was collecting championships with Dwyane Wade, Kyrie Irving and Anthony Davis. And during that first date to an Akron, Ohio Outback Steakhouse, the cheerleader and softball player had no inkling that the basketball standout from her rival high school would go on to rule the NBA. "I just thought he'd be a hometown hero for his era," she told Harper's Bazaar, "and it would be over."

Fast forward a decade or so, and she and 2003's No. 1 draft pick were married at an event so star-studded Beyoncé and Jay-Z were on hand to perform their hit "Crazy in Love."

After eight seasons in L.A., where James took his trophy-winning talents to the Lakers, he announced plans to finish his career with the Philadelphia 76ers in July 2026.

"The only reason why I can do what I do at the highest level both on and off the floor is my because my best friend got my back regardless the outcome!" he wrote in a November 2019 tribute. "I'm just the car, she's the engine!"

A two-time defensive player of the year, Los Angeles Clippers forward Kawhi Leonard is also skilled at blocking inquiries into his personal life. More than a decade into his romance with fellow San Diego State University alum Kishele Shipley, neither has even confirmed if they've wed. And fans were surprised to learn in April 2019 that the two-time champ (who, like his partner, doesn't have a public Instagram) missed a game because Shipley had given birth to their second child, son Mark Leonard.

"He doesn't give a damn about the stardom," former coach Gregg Popovich has said. Daughter Kaliyah Leonard remains unimpressed as well, the then-4-year-old choosing the Toronto Raptors' victory parade in 2019 as the perfect spot to take a nap!

Hard to believe two-time NBA MVP Steph Curry failed to connect on his initial move with now-wife Ayesha Curry. But when the then-Davidson College standout went in for a kiss during a hang with his former youth group pal, she ducked.

Thankfully, "We had a do-over!" she told told E! News' Jason Kennedy in October 2017. And a few years after that first kiss in his parents' driveway back in their hometown of Charlotte, he proposed in that very spot. "Yeah," he told Parents, "it was like The Notebook."

When they discovered months after their 2011 vows they were expecting their first child—future press conference scene-stealer Riley—Ayesha worried she'd never fully find her professional footing.

But more than a decade, three more kids—daughter Ryan joined the squad in 2015, followed by brothers Canon and Caius in 2018 and 2024—and an entire lifestyle empire later, she's done just fine, her list of titles including cookbook author, Food Network personality, model and philanthropist.

Just don't saddle her with the term "basketball wife." As she shrewdly pointed out to ABC News, "I mean, I don't think my husband would call himself 'chef's wife.'"

We love a man who stays on brand. Back in 2016, Clippers guard Bradley Beal took the beauty entrepreneur "to the top of the Ferris wheel in Vegas, and asked me to be your girlfriend," she shared on Instagram. Four years and two sons—Bradley Jr. and Braylon—he brought her to a similar ride in Maryland. "Now the second time you're on a Ferris wheel, I'm asking you to be my wife," the three-time All-Star said in clip of his January 2020 proposal.

Her answer, of course, was an unequivocal yes. "No one else id rather spend my life with," wrote the XO By Kamiah founder, who welcomed third son Braxton in 2022 ahead of their vows and fourth son Braydie in July 2026. "Thank you for helping me evolve into the woman I've become, and for constantly challenging me to become better each and everyday."

As St. Joe's best offensive player for two consecutive seasons in the mid-2000s, guard Ayahna Cornish-Lowry isn't your typical courtside cheerleader. Sharing with Canadian lifestyle site The Kit in 2019 that she prefers "to be close to the action," the mom of sons Karter Lowry and Kameron Lowry said she doesn't just zero in on her husband Kyle Lowry.

Rather she's taking in every set that his squad runs: "I don't focus in on just Kyle, I try to watch the whole game and the whole team and see what's going on. I love watching it from a basketball eye."

And she's not afraid to give the six-time All-Star and Olympic gold medalist, who announced his retirement in July 2026, her take on how he's running the floor. "He'll come up to me during time-outs, that's how close I am," she said of the point guard, her sweetheart since their days at Philadelphia's Cardinal Dougherty High. "If I see something, I try to mouth it to him. Maybe he'll get it."

Draymond Green, the Warriors' outspoken four-time All-Star isn't exactly known for his subtlety. So when he asked Hazel Renee to be his bride in January 2019, he went full court press. There was a helicopter ride to a yacht filled with their family, friends and kids Olive Jay and Draymond Jamal Green Jr., a six-carat Jason of Beverly Hills diamond and no less than Golden State coach Steve Kerr spilling the news to the press.

After sharing that he and the Empire actress were holding their vows around a planned return trip to the Olympics, COVID-19 forced them to reschedule and focus on a new milestone: Welcoming daughter Cash in October 2020.

"Our journey that we are on has been nothing short of amazing!" he wrote in a 2020 birthday tribute. "Through the good and bad times you continue to be the rock of our family."

Finally walking down the aisle in 2022 (with Vogue publishing photos from their vows), the pair welcomed daughter Hunni in 2023 and their latest arrival in Feburary 2026.

Known for racking up the points, recently retired point guard Russell Westbrook took on the role of cheerleader, hyping up bride Nina Westbrook as she nailed shot after shot in a March 2020 Instagram video. And it's not as if he was blowing hot air. Now a licensed marriage and couples therapist, Nina was once UCLA's fastest players when she spied a flashy young point guard winking at her as he nailed a breakaway dunk. "You were pretty good out there tonight," she reportedly told him after the game. "It's easy to play like that when you have someone to play for," he shot back.

More than a decade later they're juggling their Why Not? children's foundation with raising son Noah and twin daughters Skye and Jordyn and enjoying the occasional dinner-and-a-movie night in. "There is not a thing you won't do to bring a laughter and joy to our children's life," she raved in a Father's Day post. "You are the coolest dad, the definition of fun, and the embodiment of love."

At this point, it's unclear who gets more play in Sports Illustrated—the Utah Jazz big man Kevin Love or Swimsuit Issue cover girl Kate Bock, a fixture since being named Rookie of the Year in 2013. Not that her guy is feeling competitive. "This is a timeless cover," he wrote of the 2020 edition in a congratulatory post. "It could not be a better representation of the beautiful woman you are and continue to be. I'm just so happy for you."

More than a year after the five-time All-Star power forward proposed during a January 2021 birthday celebration, they wed at the New York Public Library.

"We both envisioned an old-school New York City, Great Gatbsy-inspired, black and white ball for the big day," the Love Kate founder detailed to Vogue. "That was the easy part! The hard part was just making the small detailed decisions—whether it was a specific linen, the seating chart, or where to get ready."

Soon after, they were prepping for a new era, the two welcoming daughter James in June 2023 and her younger sister Leighton on Valentine's Day 2025.

You know you're basketball royalty when your wedding party includes LeBron James and his bride. In fact, everyone from Dwyane Wade and Carmelo Anthony (plus Gabrielle Union and LaLa Anthony) to Ludacris and Kevin Hart turned out for Chris Paul and Jada Crawley's 2011 Charlotte vows, with no less than Robin Thicke providing the wedding music.

And while an in-ceremony performance by gospel legend BeBe Winans and some 10,000 roses, orchids and hydrangeas is nice, nothing is more important to the Thunder's 12-time All-Star than his top teammate.

His day one since they met at Wake Forest University, "I truly love Jada; she has been there for the ups and the downs," the recently retired point guard told Essence of the philanthropist, mom to Christopher II and Camryn. "Basketball isn't going to last forever. Jada and I love spending time with each other, genuinely."

In the Horford family, it's Al Horford's bride that truly holds court. Model and singer Amelia Vega's titles include Miss Dominican Republic 2002 and Miss Universe 2003.

Though it took two meetings, the first at the Latin Pride Awards in Boston and the second four years later working together on a campaign for children with cancer, the Dominican born five-time All-Star said he was confident early on that he'd found his forever teammate.

"We started dating and became pretty obvious that she was the right person for me. It just felt right," the Warriors power forward told Latina in 2013. "I would always make fun of people, or wouldn't believe something like that was true. I felt right with her and I knew that I wanted to marry her."

More than a decade in, "Married life is awesome," said the University of Florida standout, dad to Ean, Alía, Ava, Nova and Mila with the Miami boutique owner. "We're building something special—our lives together."

Back in 2008 when Portland Trailblazers guard Jrue Holiday was a stand-out freshman at UCLA, an autograph seeker approached him at a women's basketball game, thinking he was his teammate Darren Collison. Witnessing the whole exchange, Lauren Holiday, a member of the Bruins soccer team, chimed in, "Don't worry, you're cuter than Darren."

It's a decidedly adorable meet-cute, but the rest of their love story is even better. Retired from the national women's team, the World Cup champ and two-time gold medalist was nearly five months pregnant when she learned she had a brain tumor. Without thought, Jrue took a months-long sabbatical from his NBA gig in 2016 to be at his bride's side until the meningioma was successfully removed.

Now a devoted father to theirdaughter Jrue and son Hendricks, "You show us everyday what unconditional love looks like," Lauren wrote in a Father's Day tribute. You show up for us on your best and your worst days and it never feels like you give us any less."

Just a few years removed from his career at Butler University, now-retired forward Gordon Hayward shot his shot, asking recent high school grad Robyn Hayward to be his bride on Christmas Eve 2013. Married the following May, the athletes—she was a standout volleyball player at her Indiana high school—have steadily been putting together their own squad ever since.

Son Theo joined daughters Bernie, Charlie and Nora in September 2020 while Gordon was battling it out in the bubble with the Boston Celtics.

And despite having to play zone with all their little ones, the duo haven't ruled out bringing on more teammates. "Bernie is sweet and gentle, Charlie is always doing things on her own time and beats to her own drum, Nora makes sure Theo knows she's the boss and has no fear at all, and Theo is pretty unbothered and chill (so far)," she detailed in a December 2020 post. "This is what 4 kids 5 and under looks like (for us)... @gordonhayward do you want more kids?"

Turns out he was ready to run another play. The couple welcomed son Sebastian in September 2025.

#782. ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham

WSL’s second-highest goalscorer is likened to England legend for her crossing and has earned France call-up

At the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. It was an innocuous moment that might have escaped most onlookers at Hednesford Town’s Keys Park but it demonstrated the swagger with which she is playing.

To observe the 22-year-old warming up before the 1-1 League Cup draw at Aston Villa last week was to witness a player making skills look easy, taking one touch where others took two and pulling off no-look passes. She is backing up that panache in the Women’s Super League, as the joint second-highest goalscorer with six from the promoted side’s opening eight matches. Only Khadija Shaw has scored more.

Add in two WSL assists and a goal and an assist on her France debut last month and it has been a breakthrough campaign for Hurtré that very few expected, except perhaps those who followed closely her career in France. They include the former France head coach Olivier Echouafni, who gave a 16-year-old Hurtré her professional debut for Paris Saint-Germain during the title-winning 2020-21 campaign, the only time a side have stopped OL Lyonnes from finishing top in the past 20 years.

“She listens to everything the coach says, she’s very attentive, she’s very focused,” Echouafni says. “She’s like a sun, because when you speak with her there’s a big light. She was always quite skilful, moving the ball quickly to draw out her opponent, and had a good shot and delivered quality crosses.

“Back then, she lacked athletic stamina, the ability to sustain repeated bursts and sometimes also struggled in one-on-one situations because she was so young, but she has made great progress since then. She has also made great progress mentally – her move to Birmingham has done her a world of good.”

WSL fans are enjoying Hurtré’s pace, skill and general attacking threats, but imprinted in Echouafni’s memory are her defensive efforts as a youngster. He recalls Hurtré, on her second league appearance, against Paris FC in May 2021, replacing the Canada full-back Ashley Lawrence with two minutes remaining. “She cleared the ball off the goalline and prevented the equaliser,” he says. “It was a very important action because, one week later, PSG won the championship.”

To describe her as surrounded by experienced professionals at PSG would be a big understatement. When she had made her debut, in Europe against the Polish side Gornik Leczna, she was on the same team as a 42-year-old Formiga. Her gratitude to PSG is clear: she was spotted at the Joie Stadium last week watching Manchester City take on PSG in the Women’s Champions League, sitting just above her former club’s bench. PSG loaned Hurtré to Dijon in 2022 to gain more first-team experience and to Bordeaux in 2023-24. An injury at each affected her game time but she left a strong impression.

“I wanted to sign Océane for two main reasons,” says Sylvain Carric, Dijon women’s general manager from 2022 until 2026, who now runs the Strasbourg women’s teams. “The first was, naturally, the quality of her left foot – it’s magnificent; she can put the ball exactly where she wants it. The second was her versatility. She’s capable of playing as a left-back, a winger or a No 8.

“Océane left a fantastic impression during her time at Dijon. She had the intelligence to come to Dijon to grow, rather than remaining on the bench at PSG. She was a very good player and an excellent teammate, always smiling. She has been supported by a very good inner circle, especially her father, who I believe played an important role in her success. As for her potential, it was obvious, especially given that left foot, but she just needed to adapt her physique for the elite level. Now that she’s brought all those elements together, I’m certainly not surprised.”

Hurtré took a risk when she joined second-tier Birmingham in the summer of 2025 but it has paid off after she helped them to win promotion and she has goals against clubs including Arsenal, Brighton and Manchester City.

Birmingham’s head coach, Amy Merricks, said last month: “We’re incredibly proud of her. I’m not going to share it but, if I did share where she was when she first came in, people wouldn’t quite believe the turnaround. There were so many areas that she needed support with, transitioning to a different country at a young age. She’s learned English, which is a massive step.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

“Everyone sees her work on the pitch but we are fortunate to see the amount of work she’s done of it, and it absolutely translates. She’s diligent, she’s a student of the game, and she thoroughly deserved the call-up [for France].”

Hurtré was rewarded for her strong start with the WSL player of the month award for September. Sylvain Jamet, a women’s football writer for the French magazine footofeminin, saw her play at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Costa Rica and believes Hurtré has become “a lot faster” at Birmingham.

“Her technical ability and her set-piece deliveries with her left foot stood out,” Jamet says of Hurtré’s six years representing France’s youth teams. “Since she’s arrived in the UK, they must have worked on her speed.”

Hurtré’s goal contributions in France’s 9-0 win against Latvia have boosted her hopes of a place at the World Cup next summer. Jamet, comparing her to Chelsea’s left-sided France player Sandy Baltimore, says: “They’re competing for the same place with France now. She’s less explosive than Sandy, but she’s better technically for the crosses and passing. Baltimore’s obviously fantastic, more like a one-v-one player, taking on defenders.

“Hurtré can cross from anywhere, she can do what [David] Beckham did, basically, crossing from deep, crossing from anywhere. She had very good first cap for France. There’s a good chance she will be in the squad for the World Cup. I really expect her to get one of those 26 places.”

#781. Bournemouth’s decision not to panic after their tough start is paying off

Marco Rose’s team did not win any of their first six games in the Premier League but he stayed calm and positive

It would have been easy, understandable even, for Bournemouth fans to feel down and worried. Their revered head coach, Andoni Iraola, had left in the summer and his replacement, Marco Rose, had not got off to a great start. Three defeats and three draws was all they had to show from their first six league matches, and whispers about Rose’s future had begun in the media.

But Bournemouth fans know it can take a while for new ideas and methods to yield positive results. Iraola didn’t win any of his first nine Premier League games in charge of the club and he ended up having a remarkable impact.

Still, the outlook wasn’t great after Bournemouth were hammered 5-1 by Chelsea. But Rose maintained his level-headedness. He had been adamant until that point that Bournemouth’s performances had been better than results suggested. “It’s about results at this level. But performance-wise, I see a lot of good things,” he said.

Rose was much less understanding after the hammering at Stamford Bridge, but again there were still reasons to think the result was harsh. Chelsea’s five goals came from only 1.1 expected goals (xG). The standard of their finishing was incredibly high at times, with Jordan Henderson scoring twice from outside the box (one a free-kick) and João Pedro rifling emphatically into the roof of the net from a Pedro Neto cut-back. And Morgan Rogers’ effort was helped by a deflection. Bournemouth created opportunities, with a greater xG total (1.38) than their hosts, but ended up on the end of a hiding.

The one-sided result was something of a novelty, but the overriding sense that Bournemouth had been unlucky was familiar. Not much had gone their way in the five matches before that. In their defeat at Manchester City on the opening weekend, Bournemouth led 1-0 until the 84th minute, before losing 2-1.

In their second match of the season, they were denied by a 90th-minute equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Everton. “As a coach, you evaluate the performance as well as the result, and in most phases of the game it was really good,” Rose said. “I don’t want to blame anyone because I saw so many positive things.” Next up, an 88th-minute leveller rescued Newcastle a 2-2 draw from 2-0 down at St James’ Park. And in their fourth match of the season, Bournemouth led twice against Brentford but had to settle for a 2-2 draw after individual errors from Adrien Truffert and Djordje Petrovic.

Rose continued to focus on the positives. There was an acceptance that results needed to catch up eventually, though he liked a lot of what he was watching. “I’m really happy with the confidence the lads came here today to take the three points,” he said after the Newcastle draw. Even after the loss to Liverpool left them with only three points from a possible 15, Rose cut an optimistic figure, saying: “We played a good game against Liverpool. They had some days more to recover, and I think we looked fit, even at the end. We were the team that went for a goal.”

Bournemouth won the “xG battle” four times in their first six matches. That obviously doesn’t count for much in real terms, but it shows that they were creating more high-value opportunities than their opponents. Their position of 18th in the table was not a clear reflection of their performances. “We can see the table. Now it’s up to us to prove we can handle the situation,” Rose challenged his players after the Chelsea loss.

We can use expected points (xPts) to support the idea that Bournemouth’s position was false. Our xPts model uses xG data from each match to calculate how games “deserved” to finish based on the quality and quantity of chances at each end. Although Bournemouth were in the relegation zone with three points, their 8.4 xPts put them comfortably in mid-table.

Rose’s optimistic appraisals should not be overlooked as standard post-match managerial guff either. There’s an argument his positivity and clarity played a big role in helping the Bournemouth players appreciate they were on the right track even when results were underwhelming. The worry was the team could lose confidence and sink, but hindsight suggests the coach did well to mitigate such a threat.

Since the defeat to Chelsea, Bournemouth have played six and won six in all competitions. They have scored 16 goals from 16.4 xG and allowed their opponents chances worth only 0.81 xG on average – and, crucially, Henderson’s free-kick at Stamford Bridge was the last goal they conceded. They have beaten Sturm Graz and Milan in the Europa League, Aston Villa in the League Cup, and Sunderland, Manchester United and Leeds in the Premier League.

Their recent fixtures have been slightly kinder given they played City, Newcastle, Liverpool and Chelsea – three of which were away – during their first six Premier League outings. But Milan and Leeds both made decent starts to the season, Villa have been resurgent of late, and wins at Old Trafford can never be taken for granted.

The outlook for Bournemouth is now considerably different in the Premier League. Those three wins have lifted them to eighth in the table, and because their recent victories have been so comprehensive, they’ve absolutely shot up the xPts table as well. Only Arsenal (18.2), Man City (17.1) and Nottingham Forest (15.5) can better Bournemouth’s 15.4 xPts over the full season to date.

It’s been an impressive transformation but Rose isn’t trying to take the credit. “I would love to say I’m a magician and I changed some good stuff, but sometimes it’s just about getting this kind of experience, and then if you react well that’s always the most important thing,” he mused before the Leeds win. “You can make mistakes – you can lose, you can have a bad day – but the reaction is the most important thing, and I think we showed a good reaction. We didn’t lack much, and now we just have the last ​5​% in everything.”

Evanilson finding some form in front of goal has helped, with the Brazilian scoring in each of his past four league outings, his four goals coming from 2.8 xG. Bournemouth have also limited their opposition’s flow of high-quality chances. And their upcoming fixture list looks kind.

Over the next five matches, only Coventry and Aston Villa have more straightforward schedules than Bournemouth according to our rankings. Their climb could yet continue.

Bournemouth’s surge up the table shows how quickly a club’s fortunes can change, and it’s evidence of how patience can be rewarded when it might be easier to panic. Rose may not feel as though he has changed much, but ensuring his team retained belief when heads might have dropped is as valuable as any tactical alteration.

#779. Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?

A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

Since a ceasefire took effect in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in Ukraine's Kherson region on October 27, preparations have been underway to evacuate residents trapped there.

Following Russia's occupation of the town in 2022 and the flooding caused by the destruction of the nearby Kakhovka dam in 2023, residents were cut off from the outside world. All access routes to Oleshky, which lies on the Dnipro River, had been mined. Former Oleshky residents who managed to escape and talked to DW described hunger, no access to medicine, and no electricity or water. About 2,000 people are still living in the town.

According to the Save Ukraine Foundation, it has rescued at least 300 civilians from Oleshky over the past six months. DW spoke with lawyer Myroslava Kharchenko, who works for the organization, about preparations for the upcoming evacuation.

DW: A ceasefire is already in effect in Oleshky. Do you know whether any evacuation efforts have begun?

Myroslava Kharchenko: No, we do not have that information yet. What we do know is that the ceasefire came into effect on October 27 at 3 a.m. Kyiv time, which is 4 a.m. in Russia. Mine-clearing operations on the road began at around 8 a.m. What is happening inside Oleshky itself, however, is entirely within the military's remit. Everyone involved in this operation has been asked to maintain strict confidentiality. Any careless remark or action could jeopardize the entire evacuation effort.

What I can see is that information is being actively collected through closed internal local chat groups. Registration lists and application forms are being shared, and people are filling them out themselves. Organizers are contacting those who previously requested evacuation to verify details such as their date of birth and current place of residence. They are also asking people to provide contact information for neighbors or relatives who may be nearby or in the same building, because communications are extremely unreliable.

The organizers are also collecting information about the health conditions of those planning to leave. Among them are people who are ill, have limited mobility, or are recovering from recent injuries, including blast and mine-related wounds. We therefore expect those organizing the evacuation to ensure that medical assistance is available for those who need it.

How exactly is the evacuation expected to take place? Will people be evacuated through Russian-controlled territory or via the Dnipro River? Have any routes already been agreed upon?

As far as we know, a river route would be extremely dangerous. We have not heard any confirmation that such an option has been approved. It therefore appears likely that the evacuation route will pass through the temporarily occupied Ukrainian territory and possibly through Russia before people are able to reach Ukraine. For security reasons, however, none of these details are being made public.

What do you know about the number of people expected to be evacuated?

We are actually very pleased that the evacuation is not expected to take place in a single day. That is important because we hope that those who manage to leave safely during the first stage will serve as an example for others.

People still trapped in Oleshky are extremely afraid. There have already been numerous provocations, and this is not the first attempt to establish such a route or humanitarian corridor.

As a result, there is a great deal of suspicion. Those concerns are based largely on uncertainty, and some people may choose not to leave during the initial phase of the evacuation. Overall, however, we estimate that around 500 people may eventually be evacuated.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

How would you assess the role of Melania Trump in making this evacuation possible?

We are immensely grateful to Melania Trump for drawing attention to the humanitarian catastrophe currently unfolding in Oleshky. What is taking place there is in fact genocide committed by the Russian Federation.

We are thankful for her efforts and hope they will help make this evacuation possible. We will be even more grateful once most people are safely removed from the combat zone and arrive in Ukrainian government-controlled territory.

When could the physical evacuation of civilians begin?

I can't say how long it will take. What seems clear, however, is that time will be needed to clear mines from the roads leading into the city. We also understand that many streets inside Oleshky are mined, so additional work will be required to make routes within the city safe.

There is a hospital from which people need to be evacuated. Nearby is a morgue where bodies also need to be recovered.

I do not know whether that will be included as part of this humanitarian corridor, but it is undoubtedly important. The bodies need to be identified and the causes of death established. That process will also take time, regardless of how quickly the military is able to work.

It is difficult to make any predictions because, as you can see, everything is being conducted under strict secrecy. Statements from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides have been extremely cautious, and that is clearly justified under the circumstances.

#777. Referee hands out record 53 red cards after chaos at under-20s game in Brazil

Sendings-off include 43 players and two board members

Goal celebration is said to have sparked brawl

An under-20s match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais descended into chaos, with the referee handing out a record 53 red cards after a brawl.

The incident took place during the first leg of a state ⁠championship semi-final match between ⁠Uberlandia and ​Mamore. In his report the referee, Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto, said the trouble began early in the second half, ⁠when a number of Uberlandia officials invaded the field after one of their players was sent off.

The match was halted for 40 ⁠minutes and eventually restarted, with Mamore going on to score in the ninth minute of ​stoppage time to take a 3-1 lead.

According ‌to reports in Brazilian ‌media, the Mamore player Davi taunted Uberlandia players during the goal celebrations, which sparked a brawl and led to a deluge of red cards.

A total of 43 players and eight members of the coaching staff were sent off, and two Uberlandia board members were also dismissed.

“In the 54th minute of the second half, a generalised brawl broke out, making it impossible to show the red cards and ‌to carry out the match-closing protocol,” Drosghic Modesto wrote in his report. “Therefore, owing to all the turmoil and the lack of security, I declared ​the match ended.“

Drosghic Modesto added that a police report had been filed over threats made against him and that Mamore’s team had vandalised the dressing room after the match.

The previous Guinness world record for the most red cards shown in a match was 36, which occurred in ⁠February 2011 during a fifth-division match in Argentina between Atlético Claypole and ​Victoriano Arenas.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

On Wednesday, Uberlandia ​said it would be forfeiting the ​second leg of the semi-final in a “gesture of fair play” because Mamore ​did not have ‌enough eligible players ​to field a team. The ​forfeit means Mamore qualify for the final.

Uberlandia said: “The club has also not remained silent: the appropriate disciplinary measures regarding those involved have already been taken internally, because athletic development is, above all, a matter of personal development.”

#776. The oracle of the second quadrant

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Chao Liu has driven up and down the US East Coast — from Florida to Massachusetts — before detouring to France. His latest stop is at IFREMER, where he will continue to pretend to be a real scientist until someone finally catches on.

The machine sat between the deep-fryer truck and a three-legged goat, housed inside a canvas tent that smelled heavily of kerosene and stale popcorn. It was a massive, rivet-popped iron boiler known officially as the Differential Analytical Oscillator, although the hand-painted sign out front simply read: THE DAO BOILER — KNOWS ALL, TELLS ALL. FIVE CENTS.

By late afternoon, the fairground was a soup of churned mud and diesel exhaust.

“It don’t do lottery numbers,” the operator said, not looking up from the greasy carburettor he was scraping with a butter knife. He was a small, sour man named Silas, wearing a leather apron stiff with soot. “And if you’re gonna ask if your brother’s a bastard, save your nickel. The answer is always yes.”

Jerry shifted his boots in the sawdust. He was 19, wore a stained canvas jacket, and had spent the past three days trying to look tragically heartbroken on his front porch. “I don’t care about the lottery. I want to know about Clara.”

Silas sighed, spitting a dark stream of tobacco juice into a bucket of scrap iron. “The butcher’s girl? She left on the 4.10 rail to Lowmarsh. What’s to know? She wanted indoor plumbing and a man who didn’t smell like fertilizer.”

“No,” Jerry said, his jaw tightening as he dropped a heavy brass nickel onto the tool chest. “She said it wasn’t that. She said there was a … a fundamental misalignment in our vectors. I want to know what that means. I want the real, exact reason.”

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Silas looked at the coin, then at Jerry’s face. He let out a dry, rattling chuckle. “The exact reason? All right, kid. But the tub don’t do poetry. You want the low-voltage ribbon or the full squeeze?”

“Give me the whole thing,” Jerry said, crossing his arms. “Don’t spare the details.”

Silas shrugged, picking up a heavy, lead-lined copper helmet attached to the boiler by a thick bundle of rubber-coated cables. It looked like an old diving apparatus, dripping with mineral oil. “Put it on. Full throttle means you get the absolute breakdown. Don’t say I didn’t warn you.”

Jerry lifted the helmet. It was incredibly heavy, cold against his ears. He lowered it over his head, plunging himself into absolute darkness.

For three seconds, there was only the smell of hot grease and the rhythmic thump-thump-thump of the internal pistons. Then, the engine engaged the clutch.

The Universe didn’t open up with grand spiritual enlightenment. It opened with a relentless, deafening avalanche of raw data.

Jerry didn’t see Clara’s face, or a vision of her on the train. Instead, a cold, mechanical voice began reading a molecular ledger directly into his auditory cortex. It informed him that on Tuesday at 3.14 p.m., the atmospheric humidity had caused a 0.04% swelling in the leather of Clara’s left boot, which altered her gait by three millimetres. This structural variance, combined with the gravitational pull of a passing manure spreader, had shifted her centre of gravity exactly enough to cause a microscopic tear in the cotton fibre of her socks.

The machine kept going. It explained that the chemical composition of Jerry’s afternoon sweat contained an excess of sulfur molecules that reacted poorly with the zinc coating on his porch railing, creating a localized scent profile that her olfactory nerves categorized under Sub-Class 4: Decaying Organic Matter. It gave him the exact thermodynamic equation of the breeze that had carried the smell to her nose. It gave him the precise atomic mass of the dust particle she choked on when she tried to say goodbye.

It went on for what felt like an eternity, resolving her ‘broken heart’ into a massive, agonizingly boring list of friction coefficients, cellular degeneration rates and barometric pressure shifts. There was no love. There was no betrayal. There was only a three-hour maths problem about why a girl walked towards a train station.

The helmet was violently yanked off his head.

Jerry stumbled backwards, blinking against the harsh light of the tent. The machine was smoking, its violet glow dying back into a dull, rusted grey. Silas was standing over him, holding the helmet, looking thoroughly bored.

#774. Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football

Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine

Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier.

Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments.

“Of course, we plan to submit documents,” the Sevastopol CEO Valery Chaly told local media last month. “According to the regulations we should advance to the next stage.” The RFU remains a member of Uefa and Fifa but there would be fresh calls for it to be ejected if Sevastopol’s ascent is not blocked. It is understood no decision about their potential admission has been made.

Football’s governing bodies were given a similar dilemma in 2023 when Sevastopol and another Crimean club, Rubin Yalta, were accepted into FNL 2B even though sides from the occupied territory have not been allowed to compete in Russia since its annexation in 2014.

The Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) asked Uefa and Fifa to consider ejecting Russia, alleging a “gross violation” of their statutes and Uefa’s ruling, made in 2014, that Crimean clubs must not compete in RFU-run events. Uefa claimed it would assess the situation but the authorities appeared to turn a blind eye, the RFU saying it had created a workaround by making FNL 2B an amateur competition that it did not operate. At the time, several clubs at that level contacted by the Guardian confirmed informally that they were fully professional. No such blurring of the lines exists for FNL 2A, which has never denied its clubs are professional.

That unwillingness to act led to escalation when, in April 2024, an imitation of the Ukrainian club Zorya Luhansk – whose home city in Donbas is illegally occupied by Russia – was admitted to FNL 2B. This year they were joined by a fake Shakhtar Donetsk, mimicking the current Champions League side who have been forced to play elsewhere since 2014. Five of the 15 teams who completed the recent FNL 2B group one season played in or claimed to represent occupied areas, the Simferopol-based club Kyzyltash Bakhchisaray completing the quintet.

Should the RFS decide, of its own accord or under pressure from international bodies, to bar Sevastopol from promotion an even bigger flashpoint may await. The imitation Shakhtar finished runners-up in group 1, securing that spot by winning 2-0 at Sevastopol on the season’s final day last Saturday, and are next in line to go up. Unlike Sevastopol their home matches are played on Russian territory, in Taganrog, rather than an occupied area. The club is, however, registered to an address in Donetsk.

In October 2025 the UAF asked Uefa to review and explain the imitation clubs’ legal positions but, as with any assessment of the Crimean clubs’ participation, the results are still awaited. It warned of a“coordinated political attempt to legitimise the occupation and erase the identity of Ukrainian football”.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Last month Russia competed in a Fifa-run event for the first time since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, finishing 19th in the new under-15 World Cup. Teams at under-15 and under-16 levels have continued to play in smaller Uefa development tournaments, largely against invited opponents on home soil, during the war in Ukraine.

None of Uefa, Fifa, the RFU, the FNL, Sevastopol or the imitation Shakhtar Donetsk offered comment when contacted by the Guardian.

Max Rushden is joined by Barry Glendenning, Lars Sivertsen and Jonathan Liew as Liverpool lose for the first time in the Champions League this season and Manchester City and Arsenal escape with narrow wins

Rate, review, share on Apple Podcasts and join the conversation on email.

On the podcast today: defeat for Liverpool in Turkey with Dirk Kuyt’s Fenerbache winning by the odd goal in five. Manchester City are tested by RB Leipzig but the game was ultimately settled by a beautiful sweeping move finished off by Erling Haaland.

Elsewhere, Arsenal win 2-1 in Prague, a third away game in seven days and they looked tired. Real Madrid find a way (don’t they always) in Athens and Como score nine at Lens.

Plus, previewing the Premier League weekend, with as many as five managers worried about their jobs post international break, and your questions answered.

#769. World record 53 red cards shown in Brazilian youth game

43 players and eight members of staff received red cards after the brawl, as well as two board members

A world record of 53 red cards were shown during a chaotic under-20s game in Brazil.

The semi-final first leg of the Minas Gerais Under-20 Championship tie between Uberlandia and Mamore was marred by scenes that led to 43 players and eight members of coaching staff being sent off.

There was also two Uberlandia board members dismissed, taking the tally up to 53.

The previous record was 36, in a 2011 fifth-division game between Club Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in Argentina.

Brazilian news outlet O Tempo reported the military police were called, external because of extensive damage to the Parque do Sabia Stadium.

According to the referee's report, a brawl broke out in the second half after Mamores' Davi taunted the opposition bench during celebrations when his side went 3-1 up.

Uberlandia goalkeeping coach Paulo Sergio Dias Dos Santos ran on to the pitch to confront him, sparking clashes and the subsequent dismissals, with three players having already been sent off earlier.

The police report referenced 14 broken doors, damaged shower facilities, broken windows and that benches, tables and chairs had been destroyed.

The game was paused for approximately 40 minutes and then abandoned by referee Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto.

"In the 54th minute of the second âhalf, a generalized brawl broke out, making it impossible to show the red cards and to carry âout the â match-closing protocol," Modesto wrote in his report.

"Therefore, owing to all the turmoil and the lack of security, I declared the match ended."

Uberlandia have since confirmed, external that they have conceded the second leg of the semi-final because Mamore only have seven players available as a result of all the red cards.

They described their move as a "gesture of fair play" as Mamore would progress through to the final, and Uberlandia will instead focus on the third-place match.

"The club has also not remained silent: âthe appropriate disciplinary measures regarding those involved have already been taken internally, because athletic development is, above all, a âmatter of personal development," Uberlandia added.

#768. English female coach Kaminski reaping rewards in Norway

Laura Kaminski guided Crystal Palace to the WSL 2 title in 2024

When English manager Laura Kaminski was approached to become the head coach of Norwegian club SK Brann in January, she could not turn it down.

She jumped at the opportunity to move abroad and develop her coaching skills and is even competing for a place in the Europa Cup quarter-finals next Wednesday.

It was a decision that paid off as 10 months later, she is celebrating a Norwegian league and cup double after a dream debut season.

"My time in the city [of Bergen] has been brilliant," the 38-year-old told BBC Sport.

"I can't go to the supermarket at the minute because so many people are stopping me to wish me congratulations, which is so nice.

"I'm over the moon and it was nice to get the title done before the last game so we can relax. I thought it was going to go right to the wire.

"It's been a competitive year. I've enjoyed every minute. We had a great night with all our fans, who were waiting for us to return from Oslo."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Kaminski described it as a "hectic" year as she moved from London to Norway and away from her family to take on the Brann job.

The Englishwoman had spent over a year at Crystal Palace, where she led them to promotion to the Women's Super League in 2024.

She was sacked in February 2025 after a tough WSL season as Palace struggled to compete with better financially-backed clubs.

However, she is regarded as one of the country's brightest female managers and has added to her CV with her experiences in Norway.

"I've learned a lot. It's been chaotic - I counted that I have taken 65 flights in 11 months - so it's been exhausting, but what an experience!" added Kaminski.

"To go all the way up to the Arctic Circle and play away [games] in freezing cold conditions with horizontal snow, to beautiful days in Bergen.

"Palace was totally different to Brann. I'm at a club that expects to win the Toppserien [the Norwegian top-flight] as they believe they have invested the most.

"That's been a real challenge. The WSL is dominated by the favourites in the pack so it wasn't always the expectation to get three points against big teams [at Palace]."

Kaminski admits being away from loved ones is "hard" and she has had to be prepared to "make sacrifices" but Brann's trophy success makes it worth it.

She has also picked up new ideas for her coaching philosophy having experienced the high-risk, attack-minded football in Norway.

"Norwegian teams are almost guaranteed to concede every game because they play such attacking football with no fear, and a relentlessness to press," she added.

"That is a bit different to what I was used to. When I watched the tactical displays when I first came in, I was a little bit alarmed at what people were doing.

"But when you play against their sides, and against that [pressing], it is really difficult. It's given me a lot of fuel for the future.

"There are some really fit, fast and athletic players here. It's not a surprise that big, big clubs are coming in for them."

Laura Kaminski spent a year and a half at Crystal Palace

After a season in Norway, Kaminski believes she is a better coach.

She had spent over 15 years as an assistant manager at various clubs in the WSL 2 and WSL and a coaching role with England's under-19s before joining Palace.

But having added European experience to her CV, Kaminski hopes it will open the door to more opportunities in the future.

"I'd like to think I've got a well-rounded skillset to be able to manage at the top level. Right now, my focus is on Brann and a new chapter," said Kaminski.

"There's only two levels in England that are professional. I definitely wanted to get European exposure, which I was never going to get in England.

"At the time, I was in discussions with a few clubs but it was things that I'd done before, or the project wasn't matching.

"I knew that when I came to Brann, I was going to coach top-level players. I wanted to be at the top of the competition and I was desperate to win a trophy."

Kaminski has urged other female coaches in England to go abroad and gain experience as she believes opportunities are too few in the WSL.

A study from UK Coaching in October showed there has been a 6% decline in the overall number of female coaches in recent years.

There are currently three English female coaches in the WSL - Jo Potter at Crystal Palace, Amy Merricks at Birmingham City and Karen Hills at Charlton Athletic - and they all came up with promoted clubs this summer.

But Kaminski says she is "concerned" about where they might go next and hopes more opportunities in English men's football will open up soon.

"I ended up leaving the country to go and get what I thought I deserved and had earned the right to work in, in terms of the level," said Kaminski.

"There's more than one female out there that's capable [of working in men's football]. I don't think it's out of reach. I would always, certainly, be open to it.

"At the moment, for me, there's not enough consideration even for that opportunity to be given to female managers who are more than capable.

"I think the foundations are there for females to take the plunge but is the world of football ready? I'm unsure."

#767. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane signs new contract with Bayern through to 2029

‘I love the club, fans and the city of Munich,’ says striker

Kane has 156 goals in 161 Bayern games since 2023

England captain and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane has signed a new deal with Bayern Munich through to 2029, the German club have announced.

Kane moved to Bayern from Tottenham in 2023 for a record €100m fee and has proved a huge success, scoring 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances and leading the German club to two Bundesliga titles and a DFB Cup.

The 33-year-old was named as the world’s best male player last week after scoring a remarkable 89 goals for club and country since the start of August 2025, becoming the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in 25 years and the first Bayern player since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981 to win the award.

“I feel right at home at FC Bayern,” said Kane. “I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.”

In September, Kane became the fastest player in German history to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, doing so in 98 games to shatter the previous record set by Dieter Mueller in 1977 by 31 games.

Bayern did not disclose ⁠financial details of the agreement. However, German media reported that the extension is ​the most lucrative contract ​in the club’s history and part ​of a long-term commitment to the England captain.

“We’re absolutely delighted, because with Harry Kane we have the Ballon d’Or winner on the pitch – a team player, a leader, the best all-round striker in the world,” said Christoph Freund, Bayern’s sporting director. “We all benefit from his qualities as a player and as a person, day in, day out. FC Bayern thrives on players who never stop giving their all, even when they have already achieved the greatest of goals.”

This month Kane equalled England’s all-time men’s caps record, while nudging his international goal tally to 91 in 125 appearances.

#766. Pregnant Jen Affleck Celebrates Daughter’s Birthday Amid Divorce

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Jen Affleck shared that she was celebrating daughter Nora's 5th birthday just one day after filing for divorce from Zac Affleck.

Jen Affleck is keeping the focus on her kids.

One day after filing for divorce from husband Zac Affleck, the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star took a moment to celebrate daughter Nora’s 5th birthday with a sweet Instagram message.

Jen posted a photo of Nora to her Instagram Story Nov. 4, showing her posing with a bicycle while wearing a pink shorts and shirt set covered with Disney princesses. The room was filled with balloons, including a large balloon garland that read, “Happy Birthday.” Jen captioned the sweet picture, “I can't believe she's already 5.”

The celebration comes shortly after news broke that the 27-year-old had filed for divorce from Zac, 30, on Nov. 3 after seven years of marriage, according to Utah court records obtained by E! News.

The two first met in 2018 on the Mormon dating app Mutual and married in June 2019, six months after getting engaged. In addition to Nora, Jen and Zac are also parents to kids Luca, 3, and Penelope, 16 months, and are currently expecting their fourth child together.

Still, despite Jen’s pregnancy, the pair had been candid about the struggles they faced throughout the marriage, many of which were documented on SLOMW and its upcoming spinoff series The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, which followed Zac and Jen as they moved to Southern California.

"It’s been a lot the past couple of months, I’ll be honest," Jen admitted to People in August. "But I do feel like I’m seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and just trying to count my blessings every single day."

She’d also shared how Zac had been there for her and their kids when there was “a lot that we’ve been navigating behind closed doors,” including her struggle with prenatal depression during her first trimester.

“I could not be there for my kids, and so Zac really had to show up,” she said. “I mean, he didn’t really have a choice.”

The reality star added, “I wouldn’t have survived the first trimester without him.”

While Jen and Zac have called it quits, keep reading to see where the rest of MomTok’s relationships stand.

Taylor Frankie Paul & Dakota Mortensen: Broken Up

While Taylor Frankie Paul's romance with Dakota Mortensen—they welcomed son Ever in 2024—bloomed on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, they called it quits due to Dakota's infidelity.

"Right after Ever was born, Dakota and I were living together and in bliss with our new baby, and I was even considering engagement," Taylor—who began dating the real estate agent in July 2022—revealed during the season two premiere of the Hulu series. "And then I learned that he was lying this entire time."

Taylor was told by a woman named Jenna that she and Dakota had been intimate and he had "spent the night more than once." (He has denied the claims, writing in a September 2024 TikTok that he "never cheated.")

On the series, Taylor said that Dakota accused Jenna of instigating their affair.

"No, it was him," she emphasized in the confessional. "He said he had just kissed her on the couch. No, he went on the couch, they hooked up on the couch, and then they went to the room and they hooked up."

Since ending her romance with the Basin Tiling founder, the mom of three (she shares two kids with ex-husband Tate Paul) was set to find love once again on season 22 of The Bachelorette, but things got a bit thorny when news broke in March 2026 of an alleged confrontation between the exes weeks earlier.

A spokesperson for the Draper City Police Department confirmed to People that there was an open "domestic assault investigation," telling the outlet "allegations have been made in both directions.”

Days later, a video of a previous 2023 physical altercation between Taylor and Dakota surfaced online, prompting ABC to cancel the MomToker's season of the dating franchise.

As for Dakota, he has kicked off a romance with show guest star Shinia Powell, though he previously apologized to Taylor for hooking up with her during a season four episode.

Whitney Leavitt & Connor Leavitt: Married

Whitney Leavitt found the perfect dance partner in Connor Leavitt, whom she wed in 2016. But it wasn't always smooth sailing for the couple—who share kids Sedona, Liam and Billy—as they navigated life in the spotlight.

For instance, the Dancing With the Stars alum, who announced during her Broadway run in May 2026 that she'd be leaving Mormon Wives, had to shut down rumors about her husband's sexuality.

"Do I need to put out a sex tape, or something? Like, trust me," she said on the Off the Vine podcast in October 2024. "We're good. Everything's fine."

"I think it's because when we were going through our personal stuff—and I know you haven't seen it—but he struggled through a porn addiction," she explained. "There's a scene where one of my friends says something along the lines of how they could see how he was confused sexually."

Through the ups and downs, the reality star emphasized that she and Connor—who were 23 and 22, respectively, when they got married—are stronger than ever. In fact, they even renewed their vows in February 2026 for their 10th wedding anniversary.

"We got married really young," Conner told Brides after their ceremony. "It felt like our wedding day, as much as it was for us, it really felt like it was for our families. So we really want to do something to make it ours, and this felt like a really fun way to do it."

Married in 2019, Jen Affleck and Zac Affleck—no relation to Ben Affleck, despite jokes to the contrary—have been at the center of breakup rumors since SLOMW's debut.

In fact, their fight after Jen attended a Chippendales striptease show in Las Vegas became a focal point of the first season. The couple—who share kids Nora, Penelope and Lucas—made up, however, and the Dancing With the Stars contestant later defended their relationship.

"It can be tiring and draining, just because it gets old having to hear the same things," Jen told E! News of the speculations in November 2025. "For me, I'm like, 'People will always talk and people will always have their opinions.' I think it is frustrating for him when people don't see what's happening behind closed doors and how much work and effort he's putting in."

But while Jen announced in June 2026 that she'd be adding to their dance troupe with baby No. 4, the MomToker filed for divorce that November after seven years of marriage.

Jessi Draper & Jordan Ngatikaura: Divorced

Bumps in Jessi Draper and Jordan Ngatikaura's five-year marriage emerged after the hairstylist admitted to having an emotional affair with Vanderpump Villa's Marciano Brunette, though initially it appeared they were working towards smoother roads.

"We are back together," Jessi—who shares kids Jagger and Jovi with Jordan—told E! News in November 2025. "We're trying to work on it. Relationships are not perfect. I think a situation like ours—it's going to take time. It's not going to something that's just amazing overnight."

Sadly, the reconciliation appeared to be short-lived, with Jordan also dad to daughter Peyton from a previous relationship, filing for divorce in March 2026 after five years of marriage.

However, days later, Jessi said she was “blindsided” by his filing and accused him of rushing to submit the paperwork because “he wanted the headline first.”

Admitting that her “heart sunk” seeing the news, she explained, “because we agreed to tell our children together before filing and we haven’t done that.” (E! reached out to attorneys for Jordan for comment but haven’t heard back.)

Though Jessi told E! News that she was "just casually dating and living life," when she brought Marciano as her date to the 2026 American Music Awards in May 2026, he revealed a tattoo dedicated to her that August.

Jessi and Jordan finalized their divorce in September 2026.

Mayci didn't expect to find love with Jacob Neeley. In fact, after the unexpected death of her boyfriend Arik Mack in 2015, when she was just 14 weeks pregnant with their son Hudson, she was prepared to be a single mom.

But it all changed when she met Jacob in 2016 at age 21, whom she would marry two years later.

"After everything I'd been through, I was very guarded, but Jacob was kind and we got on really well," Mayci said in her memoir Told You So. "For a long time, we remained just friends and because we weren't really dating, I was OK with him meeting my son."

"Jacob was amazing with him, which made him appear even more attractive," she continued. "I was terrified of getting hurt again but, after four months, I couldn't deny my feelings any longer. He was kind and funny and made me feel safe."

Mayci and Jacob went on to welcome daughters Harlow in 2021 and Charli in 2025.

Demi Engemann and her husband Bret Engemann tied the knot in 2021, one year after she and Blake Corbin divorced. As the couple's relationship played out on the reality show, their sexual explorations became a major plot point after Whitney gifted Demi a box of Fruity Pebbles.

The truth behind the joke gift wasn't revealed until Jessi shared on Instagram in November 2025 that "grandpa Bret likes to drink her piss like it's dirty soda and he gulps it down like water."

But Demi and Bret aren't crying over spilled secrets—or pee. In fact, she told Entertainment Tonight that December that she and Bret "have nothing else left to do other than own it and have fun with it."

Although their sex life raised eyebrows, the couple has been embracing life with their blended family. While Demi shares daughter Maude with her ex, Bret is dad to his and The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City alum Angie Harrington's sons Rome and Cole.

"I've never seen a dad so involved or love their kids harder, the most devoted step-dad to Maude, and future father to our own children one day," Demi wrote on Instagram in June 2024. "Your ability to remain consistently loyal to your role as father/step-father while navigating all that life throws your way, will never cease to amaze me!"

Mikayla Matthews and Jace Terry have been through it all together. While The reality star first met Jace in 2015 when she was 15 and they welcomed their first son Beckham two years later. Since then, the couple—who tied the knot in 2018—welcomed kids Haven, Tommie and Lottie.

While Mikayla and Jace have been loving life with their four kids, Mikayla admitted that she hopes to grow their family even further.

"When people ask me how many kids I want, I'm like, 'I've always wanted three or four, but I could see myself having six,'" she told People in February 2025. "I'm excited to hopefully move into a new house. I want a big lot for my herd of kids."

However, Mikayla confirmed in the ninth episode of the show's fourth season that she and Jace were taking time apart amid ongoing intimacy struggles.

As Mikayla began unpacking her trauma surrounding years of sexual abuse as a teen, as well as her chronic illness—which causes flare-ups due to heightened stress—their marriage had been deeply affected.

"I think it's hard anytime you bring up the stuff with the sex or the intimacy," she admitted to Jace. "I feel like it's hard on me 'cause I feel like, again, my nervous system's already in fight or flight and I'm already maxed out. My bucket is full."

After Layla Taylor and Clayton Wessel—who are parents to sons Oliver and Maxwell—divorced in 2023, the reality star teased her new romance with Mason McWhorter in July 2025.

Their relationship was a bit complicated on paper. Hang with us: Mason's brother is Chase McWhorter, the ex-husband of Layla's costar Miranda McWhorter. But the pair had been willing to put their romance to the test.

"Right now, I'm kind of scared of marriage but I just want to get to know somebody very well before I even consider that," Layla told Us in November 2025. "I'm just happy and content where me and Mason are. And if somehow that ever were to come up, then we would see."

Unfortunately, the mom of two confirmed that she and Mason had split in February 2026.

"I think we were just on two different paths right now, and he felt in order for him to grow, he had to be on his own," Layla shared. "I respect his decision, and I truly hope that he gets what he wants in life."

As for Layla, who came out as bisexual in June 2026, she soft-launched her romance with a mystery woman a month later in an Instagram video. She later seemed to confirm her relationship with Colorado-based content creator Kelsie Chesser.

Miranda McWhorter & Chase McWhorter: Divorced

Although Miranda is a newer addition to The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, joining in season two, she played a major role in the infamous MomTok "soft swinging scandal." Despite the situation with Taylor, Miranda revealed that drama wasn't the reason for her 2024 divorce from Chase.

"The reasons why we decided to split were things that were issues far before that,” she explained on the Weekly Trash podcast in August 2024. "That might not have helped, for sure, but it definitely did not play a part in the decision process."

Nonetheless, she and Chase have been committed to parenting their kids Brooks and Cohen.

"With co-parenting, you're always having to work on it," she reflected. “The thing is that if we got along perfectly all the time and it was just rainbows and butterflies, we probably wouldn't have gotten divorced."

"The thing with him and I," she continued, "we've always had a pretty good foundation of a friendship prior to even having a romantic relationship. I feel like that's something that set us up for some level of success when it comes to co-parenting."
